mw-gonna-hafta.text: We're gonna hafta push the review to Thursday.

mw-hard-stop.text: Just a heads-up, I've got a hard stop at eleven.

mw-have-you-had.text: Have ya had a chance ta look at the contract?

mw-headcount.text: We're down to forty for the offsite, so book a room for forty-five to be safe.

mw-keep-in-mind.text: We'll definitely keep you in mind for future projects.

mw-learning-curve.text: Don't worry, everyone's a little lost their first month. It's a steep learning curve.

mw-let-you-know.text: Camping? In February? Yeah... I'll let you know.

mw-loop-in.text: Could you loop me in on the thread with the design team?

mw-marathon.text: I finished in four-twelve. My goal was under four, so... next year.

mw-must-have.text: She musta left already. Her coat's gone.

mw-my-shout.text: Put your wallet away. I got this.

mw-not-saying.text: I'm not saying she's the reason they split up. I'm just saying the timing's interesting.

mw-offline.text: Let's take this offline. We're running over.

mw-oven.text: Bake it at three-fifty for twenty-five minutes. Actually, make it twenty, my oven runs hot.

mw-overrated.text: Between you and me, I thought it was a little overrated.

mw-owe-you.text: I owe you one for covering my shift. Seriously.

mw-perfectionist.text: Your résumé says you're a perfectionist. We'll see how long that lasts here.

mw-popping-round.text: My mom's 'just stopping by' on Sunday. So, you know, maybe clean up the guest room?

mw-push-back.text: The client wants to push the launch back. Again.

mw-q2.text: Sales were up eight percent in Q three. Sorry, Q two. Q three was flat.

mw-rain-check.text: Mind if I take a rain check on drinks tonight? I'm beat.

mw-rammed.text: Sorry, sorry, the subway was packed. Have you been waiting long?

mw-rent.text: Rent's twenty-four hundred a month, so eight hundred each. Plus utilities, so more like nine-fifty.

mw-reply-all.text: Did you just reply-all to the entire company?

mw-salary.text: The position starts at seventy-two K, going up to seventy-eight K after your first ninety days.

mw-sanity-check.text: Would you mind giving my deck a quick sanity check before I send it?

mw-score.text: We were up five-two in the seventh and lost six-five. Don't ask.

mw-seen-better.text: The soundtrack was great. The rest of it... I've seen better.

mw-set-up.text: So my friend wants to set you up with her cousin. Interested?

mw-shouldnt-have.text: You shouldn't've told 'im about the party.

mw-spill.text: Okay, spill. What happened with you and the guy from the climbing gym?

mw-still-sharing.text: Sorry, I think you might still be sharing your screen. Including your messages.

mw-surprise-time.text: We're setting up at seven, so don't come before half past. She gets there at quarter to eight.

mw-talk-me-through.text: So, talk me through a time something didn't go to plan.

mw-that-person.text: I hate to be that person, but you did say you'd be here by seven.

mw-the-16th.text: Can we say the thirteenth? No, wait, that's a Friday. Let's make it the sixteenth.

mw-ticket.text: Have you tried logging out and back in? If that doesn't work, I'll open a ticket.

mw-tickets.text: Tickets were eighty-five bucks each, but with fees it came to two-ten for both.

mw-time-zone.text: The call's at seven p.m. our time, so that's nine a.m. for you in Tokyo. Wait, no, eight. We're on daylight saving time.

mw-top-of-list.text: It's on my list. It's just, you know, not exactly at the top of it.

mw-under-budget.text: We came in at one point two million, about fifteen percent under budget.

mw-used-to.text: I useta play in a band, believe it or not.

mw-very-brave.text: Launching in December? Wow. That's... ambitious.

mw-werent-we.text: Weren't we s'posed to hear back by now?

mw-whaddaya.text: Whaddaya wanna do about the printer?

mw-where-at.text: Remind me, where're we at with the Kobe proposal?

mw-ya-gonna.text: Ya gonna watch the game tonight?

mw-you-made-this.text: Wait, you made this? This is seriously good.

mw-youd-better.text: Ya better book it now. It'll sell out.

n1-birthday-1.text: My birthday is on the thirteenth.

n1-birthday-2.text: My birthday is on the sixteenth.

n1-birthday-3.text: My birthday is on the nineteenth.

n1-price-1.text: That'll be fifteen hundred Bells, please.

n1-price-2.text: That'll be eight hundred Bells, please.

n1-price-3.text: That'll be four thousand Bells, please.

n1-reps-1.text: Come on, let's do fifteen push-ups!

n1-reps-2.text: Come on, let's do thirteen push-ups!

n1-reps-3.text: Come on, let's do forty push-ups!

n2-days-1.text: I've been on this island for fourteen days.

n2-days-2.text: I've been on this island for seventeen days.

n2-flight-1.text: Your flight leaves at eight forty.

n2-flight-2.text: Your flight leaves at eleven fifteen.

n2-opens-1.text: The museum opens at a quarter after nine.

n2-opens-2.text: The museum opens at a quarter to seven.

n2-opens-3.text: The museum opens at half past three.

n2-price-1.text: It's twelve thousand five hundred Bells for this one.

n2-price-2.text: It's thirty-eight thousand Bells for this one.

n2-price-3.text: It's nine thousand nine hundred Bells for this one.

n2-run-1.text: I biked sixteen miles this morning!

n2-tourney-1.text: The fishing tourney is on the thirteenth.

n2-tourney-2.text: The fishing tourney is on the thirty-first.

n3-loan-1.text: Your home loan comes to ninety-eight thousand Bells, yes, yes.

n3-meet-1.text: Meet me at ten to six, okay?

n3-meet-2.text: Meet me at twenty-five after four, okay?

n3-meet-3.text: Meet me at a quarter of eight, okay?

n3-meteor-1.text: I think the meteor shower's on the twenty-third.

n3-meteor-2.text: I think the meteor shower's on the twelfth.

n3-reps-1.text: Hold a plank for sixty seconds. Actually, no, make it ninety!

n3-reps-2.text: Hold a plank for sixty seconds. Actually, no, make it seventy!

n3-steal-1.text: It's a steal at one hundred fifteen thousand Bells!

n3-steal-2.text: It's a steal at forty-eight thousand eight hundred Bells!

n3-steal-3.text: It's a steal at sixteen thousand six hundred Bells!

n3-turnips-1.text: These turnips are a hundred and ten Bells each.

n3-turnips-2.text: These turnips are ninety-eight Bells each.

n4-claim.text: Just a reminder: we need the claim by the thirtieth, which is this Thursday.

n4-dollars.text: Parts and labor, you're lookin' at about three-forty.

n4-flight.text: You're rebooked on the nine-oh-five, flight seven six two, connecting through Chicago.

n4-gate.text: Flight eight fifteen to Denver is now boarding at gate fifty. Sorry — gate fifteen.

n4-half-nine.text: I've got Tuesday at a quarter to five, or Wednesday at a quarter after nine.

n4-highs.text: In Tokyo, expect highs of thirteen, dropping to around three overnight.

n4-platform.text: The helmet's forty bucks, so with tax you're lookin' at forty-three twenty.

n4-pounds.text: That comes to eight forty-nine. D'you need a bag?

n4-reference.text: Your confirmation number is four-seven-oh, nine-two.

n4-reps.text: Three sets of twelve. Actually, let's make it fifteen.

n4-split.text: So that's forty-six eighty for your concert ticket, with fees. Call it forty-seven. Just Venmo me whenever.

n4-water.text: Each box covers about ten square feet. For your bathroom, that's five boxes, plus one extra for breakage.

n4-yen.text: It'd be sixty-eight thousand yen, plus another five thousand if you need us to pack.

news-art-fair-1.text: Good morning, island! Let's get right to the news.

news-art-fair-2.text: First up, the autumn art fair opens at the plaza this weekend, with paintings, pottery, and photos made by residents.

news-art-fair-3.text: Organizers first said there would be fifteen booths, but they've now confirmed eighteen, so the fair will spill over onto the beach path.

news-art-fair-4.text: Visitors can vote for their favorite piece, and the winner will hang in the town hall.

news-art-fair-5.text: Turning to the city, with the sun setting earlier, Tokyo police are reminding cyclists to turn on their lights.

news-art-fair-6.text: Riding without a light after dark isn't just risky; it can also get you stopped and warned.

news-art-fair-7.text: Officials also ask riders to keep to the left and never to use a phone or umbrella while riding.

news-beach-sweep-1.text: Good morning. I'm Isabelle, and here's your island update.

news-beach-sweep-2.text: First up, residents are invited to the summer beach cleanup, which has moved from the north beach to the south beach this year.

news-beach-sweep-3.text: Volunteers will meet by the lighthouse at six-thirty, before the sand gets too hot.

news-beach-sweep-4.text: Last year's cleanup collected over thirty bags of trash, and organizers hope to beat that number.

news-beach-sweep-5.text: Turning to the city, the humid summer months make laundry a challenge for many Tokyo households.

news-beach-sweep-6.text: Clothes dried indoors can develop a musty smell, so experts suggest running a fan or a dehumidifier nearby.

news-beach-sweep-7.text: Leaving space between items helps too, as does washing smaller loads more often.

news-beach-sweep-8.text: And if you hang laundry on your balcony, keep an eye out for sudden afternoon downpours.

news-bird-count-1.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's start with what's new on the island.

news-bird-count-2.text: First up, the museum is asking residents to help with its winter bird count, which takes place over three mornings.

news-bird-count-3.text: Volunteers should meet at the museum entrance, not at the pond, and then walk there together.

news-bird-count-4.text: Binoculars can be borrowed, but bring warm gloves, since you'll be standing still for a while.

news-bird-count-5.text: Turning to the city, snow is rare in Tokyo, but even a light dusting can slow trains and snarl traffic.

news-bird-count-6.text: On days when snow is in the forecast, officials suggest leaving early or working from home if you can.

news-bird-count-7.text: Shoes with good grip make a big difference, since sidewalks and station stairs can get icy.

news-bird-count-8.text: And walk in small steps; most snow-day injuries in the city come from falls.

news-bridge-work-1.text: Good morning. Isabelle here, with the news you need before you head out.

news-bridge-work-2.text: First up, the east bridge over the river will close for repairs starting tomorrow, and the work is expected to take three days.

news-bridge-work-3.text: Residents heading to the beach should use the west bridge instead, or the small footbridge near the museum.

news-bridge-work-4.text: Officials apologize for the trouble and say the bridge will reopen with new railings.

news-bridge-work-5.text: Turning to the city, train delays are part of life in Tokyo, but there's a way to show you weren't at fault.

news-bridge-work-6.text: When a train runs late, station staff often hand out delay certificates at the gates, and many are also posted online.

news-bridge-work-7.text: Many schools and employers accept them, so grab one if you're going to be late.

news-butterfly-hall-1.text: Good morning. I'm Isabelle, and this is your island morning news.

news-butterfly-hall-2.text: First up, the museum's insect hall has opened a new spring exhibit on butterflies, and residents are already lining up.

news-butterfly-hall-3.text: The exhibit runs through the end of spring, and admission, as always, is free.

news-butterfly-hall-4.text: Guided tours start at ten each morning; an earlier notice said eleven, but that was a mistake.

news-butterfly-hall-5.text: In other news from the city, spring brings a wave of new students and employees onto Tokyo's morning trains.

news-butterfly-hall-6.text: Rail staff remind riders to take backpacks off and hold them in front, so there's room for everyone.

news-butterfly-hall-7.text: They also ask passengers to move toward the center of the car instead of crowding near the doors.

news-butterfly-hall-8.text: And if you're new in town, leaving even ten minutes early can make the ride a lot less stressful.

news-cafe-summer-1.text: Good morning, and welcome to the island news.

news-cafe-summer-2.text: First up, the café is switching to summer hours, opening an hour earlier, at seven, and closing at eight in the evening.

news-cafe-summer-3.text: The owner is also adding iced coffee to the menu, which, he says, has been the most requested drink all year.

news-cafe-summer-4.text: He's also looking for a part-time helper during the busy afternoon hours.

news-cafe-summer-5.text: Turning to the city, summer and early fall are typhoon season, and officials urge Tokyo residents to prepare now.

news-cafe-summer-6.text: That means bringing in anything on your balcony that could blow away, like plant pots or drying racks.

news-cafe-summer-7.text: It's also a good idea to keep a flashlight, drinking water, and a charged phone battery close at hand.

news-cafe-summer-8.text: And check your ward's hazard map to see whether your area is at risk of flooding.

news-cliff-trail-1.text: Good morning, and welcome to the island morning news.

news-cliff-trail-2.text: First up, a new walking trail along the cliffs is now open, linking the lighthouse to the waterfall on the north side.

news-cliff-trail-3.text: The full loop takes about forty-five minutes, though one resident told me she did it in thirty-five.

news-cliff-trail-4.text: Officials ask walkers to stay on the marked path and to keep an eye on children near the edge.

news-cliff-trail-5.text: Turning to the city, Tokyo's convenience stores do a lot more than sell snacks.

news-cliff-trail-6.text: At many locations, you can pay utility bills, send packages, and print documents, often around the clock.

news-cliff-trail-7.text: Some machines even let residents print certain ward documents with an ID card, which can save a trip to the ward office.

news-cliff-trail-8.text: Just check the hours, since that service isn't always available late at night.

news-desk-hours-1.text: Good morning. It's Isabelle, with your morning update from the island.

news-desk-hours-2.text: First up, the town hall's front desk will open earlier starting next week, at eight-thirty instead of nine.

news-desk-hours-3.text: The change is meant to help residents who stop by on their way to work or fishing.

news-desk-hours-4.text: Closing time stays the same, at five, and the desk will still close for lunch at noon.

news-desk-hours-5.text: Turning to the city, police are reminding Tokyo cyclists that every bike should be registered when it's bought.

news-desk-hours-6.text: Registration is usually done at the shop, and it makes it much easier to get a stolen bike back.

news-desk-hours-7.text: Officials are also urging riders of all ages to wear a helmet, not just children.

news-desk-hours-8.text: And if you buy a used bike, ask whether the registration has been transferred.

news-ferry-times-1.text: Good morning, and happy Sunday. I'm Isabelle, and here's your island news.

news-ferry-times-2.text: First up, the ferry to the mainland has a new schedule starting next week, with one extra trip each afternoon.

news-ferry-times-3.text: The last boat will now leave the dock at six-fifty, instead of six-fifteen, giving shoppers more time in town.

news-ferry-times-4.text: New timetables are posted at the dock and at the town hall.

news-ferry-times-5.text: Turning to the city, if you're getting rid of furniture in Tokyo, you can't just leave it out with the regular trash.

news-ferry-times-6.text: Most wards require you to book an oversized garbage pickup in advance, by phone or online.

news-ferry-times-7.text: You'll then buy a sticker at a convenience store, attach it to the item, and put it out on the assigned morning.

news-ferry-times-8.text: Pickup dates can be a week or more away, so plan ahead before a move.

news-fireworks-1.text: Good morning, and thanks for joining me. I'm Isabelle.

news-fireworks-2.text: First up, the island's summer fireworks show is back, and this year it will be held over the water by the pier.

news-fireworks-3.text: The show lasts fifteen minutes, not fifty, as some residents had heard, so don't be late.

news-fireworks-4.text: Food stands will open on the beach in the afternoon, and the museum will stay open late.

news-fireworks-5.text: Meanwhile in the city, if you find Tokyo trains too cold in summer, rail officials have a tip.

news-fireworks-6.text: Many lines run one or two mildly air-conditioned cars, often marked with a sticker on the window.

news-fireworks-7.text: These cars are kept a little warmer, which can help riders who feel chilly after coming in from the heat.

news-fireworks-8.text: And a light jacket in your bag can make a long ride much more comfortable.

news-fishing-derby-1.text: Good morning, and happy Friday! I'm Isabelle, and here's what's happening on the island.

news-fishing-derby-2.text: First up, the summer fishing contest kicks off tomorrow on the pier, and anyone with a fishing rod can join.

news-fishing-derby-3.text: Registration opens at six, not seven as in past years, and the contest runs until noon.

news-fishing-derby-4.text: Prizes go to the three biggest catches, and organizers are asking everyone to release small fish.

news-fishing-derby-5.text: Turning to the city, Tokyo officials are reminding residents that heatstroke can strike indoors, not just outside.

news-fishing-derby-6.text: Many cases involve older people at home, so check on elderly neighbors and family members when you can.

news-fishing-derby-7.text: Doctors suggest drinking water before you feel thirsty and using air conditioning, even at night.

news-fishing-derby-8.text: And if someone feels dizzy or confused, move them somewhere cool and call for help right away.

news-flea-market-1.text: Good morning, and happy Monday. I'm Isabelle, and here's what's happening on the island.

news-flea-market-2.text: First up, the spring flea market returns to the plaza this weekend, with about twenty residents signed up to sell.

news-flea-market-3.text: The market, which used to open at nine, will now start at eight-thirty, so sellers should plan to arrive early.

news-flea-market-4.text: Organizers are asking shoppers to bring their own bags.

news-flea-market-5.text: Turning to the city, spring is moving season in Tokyo, and that means long waits at many ward offices.

news-flea-market-6.text: Officials remind new residents to file their moving-in paperwork within two weeks of arriving at a new address.

news-flea-market-7.text: Mornings tend to be busiest, so if you can, plan your visit for the early afternoon instead.

news-flea-market-8.text: And don't forget a photo ID; without one, the counter may not be able to help you.

news-fossil-week-1.text: Good morning. Here's your island news, read by me, Isabelle.

news-fossil-week-2.text: First up, the museum is holding a fossil week, and residents can bring in fossils they've dug up to be identified.

news-fossil-week-3.text: The curator will look at up to thirty fossils a day, not thirteen, so there should be time for everyone.

news-fossil-week-4.text: Fossils that aren't already in the collection may be put on display, with the finder's name on the label.

news-fossil-week-5.text: Turning to the city, cooler autumn days mean more Tokyo residents are heading to the mountains for day hikes.

news-fossil-week-6.text: Trains toward popular trails can be packed on weekend mornings, so consider going on a weekday if you can.

news-fossil-week-7.text: Days get shorter this time of year, so start early and plan to be back down before dark.

news-fossil-week-8.text: Even on easy trails, bring water and a warm layer.

news-garden-plots-1.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the island news.

news-garden-plots-2.text: First up, sign-ups for the community garden open today, and this year there are twelve plots instead of eight.

news-garden-plots-3.text: Plots go to the first residents who sign up at the town hall, so organizers suggest stopping by early.

news-garden-plots-4.text: Seeds and watering cans will be provided, but gardeners are asked to bring their own gloves.

news-garden-plots-5.text: Turning to the city, pollen is a major concern for many Tokyo residents this time of year.

news-garden-plots-6.text: Doctors suggest wearing a mask outdoors and changing your clothes as soon as you get home.

news-garden-plots-7.text: They also recommend drying laundry indoors, since sheets hung outside can collect pollen in just a few hours.

news-garden-plots-8.text: If symptoms get worse, many clinics can help, but appointments fill up fast, so call ahead.

news-hama-apple-day-1.text: Good morning, and happy autumn. I'm Isabelle.

news-hama-apple-day-2.text: The apple trees by the river are full of apples.

news-hama-apple-day-3.text: This weekend, you can pick them for free.

news-hama-apple-day-4.text: Please take only five apples, so there are enough for everyone.

news-hama-apple-day-5.text: In Tokyo, autumn is a good time to get some exercise.

news-hama-apple-day-6.text: Many wards have a sports center with a gym and a pool.

news-hama-apple-day-7.text: One visit is about four hundred yen, and you don't need to sign up.

news-hama-apple-day-8.text: Most centers are open until nine at night.

news-hama-apple-day-9.text: But many are closed on Mondays, so check first.

news-hama-boat-tour-1.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to a sunny spring day.

news-hama-boat-tour-2.text: Starting today, Kapp'n has a boat tour around the island.

news-hama-boat-tour-3.text: The boat leaves the dock every day at two-fifteen.

news-hama-boat-tour-4.text: The tour takes one hour, and Kapp'n sings for you on the way.

news-hama-boat-tour-5.text: In Tokyo, it is easy to find free Wi-Fi.

news-hama-boat-tour-6.text: Many stations, cafes and convenience stores have it.

news-hama-boat-tour-7.text: You often sign in with an email address.

news-hama-boat-tour-8.text: Some places give you only thirty minutes at a time.

news-hama-boat-tour-9.text: Please don't use it to pay or to check your bank account.

news-hama-countdown-1.text: Good morning. It's Isabelle, and the year is almost over.

news-hama-countdown-2.text: On New Year's Eve, there is a countdown party in the plaza.

news-hama-countdown-3.text: It starts at eleven at night, and there is free hot soup.

news-hama-countdown-4.text: Please dress warmly, and walk carefully if there is ice.

news-hama-countdown-5.text: In Tokyo, a public bath is a nice way to warm up in winter.

news-hama-countdown-6.text: An adult pays about five hundred and fifty yen.

news-hama-countdown-7.text: Bring a small towel, or buy one at the front desk.

news-hama-countdown-8.text: Wash your body first, and then get in the bath.

news-hama-countdown-9.text: Many baths close one day a week, so check before you go.

news-hama-egg-hunt-1.text: Good morning! It's Isabelle with your island news.

news-hama-egg-hunt-10.text: You can return them in a box by the front door, even at night.

news-hama-egg-hunt-2.text: Bunny Day is this Sunday, and there is an egg hunt for everyone.

news-hama-egg-hunt-3.text: The eggs are in the trees, in the sand and under rocks.

news-hama-egg-hunt-4.text: The hunt starts at ten and ends at noon.

news-hama-egg-hunt-5.text: Bring a basket, because you may find a lot of eggs.

news-hama-egg-hunt-6.text: In Tokyo, many city libraries now have self-checkout machines.

news-hama-egg-hunt-7.text: You put your books on the machine, and it reads them all at once.

news-hama-egg-hunt-8.text: Then you get a receipt with the return date.

news-hama-egg-hunt-9.text: Most books are due in fourteen days.

news-hama-parcel-time-1.text: Good morning, everyone. It's Isabelle, and it's a cold one today.

news-hama-parcel-time-10.text: Many stores keep your box for about one week.

news-hama-parcel-time-2.text: Tonight, there is a small winter market in the plaza.

news-hama-parcel-time-3.text: It opens at five and closes at eight-thirty.

news-hama-parcel-time-4.text: You can buy warm hats, candles and sweet bread.

news-hama-parcel-time-5.text: Hot tea is free, so please come and stay warm.

news-hama-parcel-time-6.text: In Tokyo, many people get packages at the end of the year.

news-hama-parcel-time-7.text: If a box needs your signature, the driver can't leave it outside.

news-hama-parcel-time-8.text: But you can pick a new time on your phone.

news-hama-parcel-time-9.text: You can also pick it up at a convenience store near you.

news-hama-post-office-1.text: Good morning. Isabelle here, with a short island update.

news-hama-post-office-10.text: The machines are often near the door, on the left.

news-hama-post-office-2.text: The museum is closed today, because the workers are cleaning the floors.

news-hama-post-office-3.text: It opens again on Thursday morning at ten.

news-hama-post-office-4.text: The shop and the tailors are open as usual.

news-hama-post-office-5.text: Blathers says thank you, and he hopes to see you there.

news-hama-post-office-6.text: In the city, sending a letter abroad is now a little easier.

news-hama-post-office-7.text: Many post offices now have a machine for stamps and labels.

news-hama-post-office-8.text: You can pay by card, and it speaks English, too.

news-hama-post-office-9.text: If you need help, you can still ask at the counter.

news-hama-quiz-night-1.text: Good morning, and thank you for listening. This is Isabelle.

news-hama-quiz-night-2.text: On Friday night, the cafe has a quiz night.

news-hama-quiz-night-3.text: Teams of two or three can play, and it starts at seven-thirty.

news-hama-quiz-night-4.text: The winners get free coffee for one week.

news-hama-quiz-night-5.text: In Tokyo, taking a taxi is easy, even if you don't speak Japanese.

news-hama-quiz-night-6.text: Most taxis take cards, and many take train cards, too.

news-hama-quiz-night-7.text: The back door opens and closes by itself, so don't touch it.

news-hama-quiz-night-8.text: You don't need to write the address down. Just show the map on your phone.

news-hama-shell-walk-1.text: Good morning, everyone. This is Isabelle with the island news.

news-hama-shell-walk-10.text: Most pools close at six in the evening.

news-hama-shell-walk-2.text: This Sunday, there is a seashell walk on the south beach.

news-hama-shell-walk-3.text: We meet near the big rock at eight in the morning.

news-hama-shell-walk-4.text: You can keep three shells, and the rest go to the museum.

news-hama-shell-walk-5.text: Please bring a hat and some water. It will be hot.

news-hama-shell-walk-6.text: In Tokyo, the big outdoor pools open for the summer this week.

news-hama-shell-walk-7.text: A ticket for one adult is about fifteen hundred yen.

news-hama-shell-walk-8.text: Children under six can swim for free, but they need an adult.

news-hama-shell-walk-9.text: The pools are busy on weekends, so try to go early.

news-hama-shoe-visit-1.text: Good morning, everyone. It's Isabelle with today's island news.

news-hama-shoe-visit-2.text: Kicks is visiting the plaza on Thursday with shoes and bags.

news-hama-shoe-visit-3.text: He is here from nine in the morning until six.

news-hama-shoe-visit-4.text: He only comes once a month, so don't miss him.

news-hama-shoe-visit-5.text: In Tokyo, you can hear a song on the street on cold autumn nights.

news-hama-shoe-visit-6.text: It comes from a small truck that sells hot sweet potatoes.

news-hama-shoe-visit-7.text: One potato is about five hundred yen.

news-hama-shoe-visit-8.text: Some supermarkets sell them too, near the front door.

news-hama-tailor-sale-1.text: Hello, everyone, and good morning from the island.

news-hama-tailor-sale-2.text: The tailor shop has a summer sale this week.

news-hama-tailor-sale-3.text: T-shirts and summer hats are half price until Friday.

news-hama-tailor-sale-4.text: The shop is busy in the afternoon, so try to come in the morning.

news-hama-tailor-sale-5.text: In Tokyo, June is the rainy season.

news-hama-tailor-sale-6.text: If you forget your umbrella, you can rent one at some stations and stores.

news-hama-tailor-sale-7.text: You use an app on your phone, and it costs about a hundred and forty yen a day.

news-hama-tailor-sale-8.text: You can give it back at a different place, too.

news-hama-tailor-sale-9.text: So you don't need to buy a new one every time it rains.

news-hama-trash-break-1.text: Good morning, everyone. It's a dark and chilly morning.

news-hama-trash-break-2.text: From today, the cafe opens one hour early, at seven.

news-hama-trash-break-3.text: This is for people who walk to work in the cold.

news-hama-trash-break-4.text: The early hours end in March, when it gets warm again.

news-hama-trash-break-5.text: In Tokyo, trash pickup takes a break at the New Year.

news-hama-trash-break-6.text: In many wards, there is no pickup from December thirty-first.

news-hama-trash-break-7.text: It starts again on January fourth.

news-hama-trash-break-8.text: Please keep your trash inside until then, and don't put it out early.

news-hama-tree-day-1.text: Good morning, island. This is Isabelle.

news-hama-tree-day-10.text: The best time to look is after seven at night.

news-hama-tree-day-2.text: Next Saturday is tree day, and we want to plant thirty new trees.

news-hama-tree-day-3.text: Leif will give each person one small tree for free.

news-hama-tree-day-4.text: We start at nine, near the river.

news-hama-tree-day-5.text: Please wear old shoes, because the ground is wet.

news-hama-tree-day-6.text: In Tokyo, many supermarkets put stickers on food in the evening.

news-hama-tree-day-7.text: A red or yellow sticker means the price is lower.

news-hama-tree-day-8.text: Some food is twenty percent off, and some is half price.

news-hama-tree-day-9.text: It saves you money, and less food goes in the trash.

news-help-board-1.text: Good morning, and thanks for tuning in. Here's what's new around the island.

news-help-board-2.text: First up, the town hall has put up a new job board, where residents can post small tasks and offer to help each other.

news-help-board-3.text: So far there are nineteen requests, not nine as I said yesterday, so helpers are clearly needed.

news-help-board-4.text: Most of them involve carrying furniture or watering gardens while neighbors are away.

news-help-board-5.text: Turning to the city, a reminder about plastic bottles, one of the most common recycling mistakes in Tokyo.

news-help-board-6.text: Officials ask residents to remove the caps and labels, which usually go out with plastics, not with the bottles.

news-help-board-7.text: Then give the bottles a quick rinse and crush them if you can, so more fit in each bag.

news-help-board-8.text: Collection days differ by ward, so check your local schedule.

news-hoshi-campsite-1.text: Good morning, everyone. Demand for the campsite has outstripped supply this summer, so weekend spots will now be allocated by lottery.

news-hoshi-campsite-2.text: Residents who haven't stayed yet this season get two entries instead of one, which the council hopes will spread the spots around more fairly.

news-hoshi-campsite-3.text: Weekday stays remain first come, first served, and frankly, they're rarely full.

news-hoshi-campsite-4.text: The first draw is on Thursday, and winners have forty-eight hours to confirm, or the spot goes to the next name on the list.

news-hoshi-campsite-5.text: Turning to the city, if you're counting on your credit card's travel insurance for a trip abroad this summer, it may be worth double-checking the terms.

news-hoshi-campsite-6.text: Many cards now cover you only if the trip itself, typically the airfare or a tour, was charged to that card.

news-hoshi-campsite-7.text: Even then, the medical limit can be modest, a real concern in the United States, where a short hospital stay can run into millions of yen.

news-hoshi-campsite-8.text: Advisers suggest topping it up with a separate policy, rather than assuming you're fully covered.

news-hoshi-card-refund-1.text: Good morning. The tailor shop is bringing back its made-to-order service, after a break of nearly a year.

news-hoshi-card-refund-2.text: Orders take about three weeks, and a deposit of half the price is required up front.

news-hoshi-card-refund-3.text: Sable says the deposit can be returned if you change your mind, but only until the fabric has been cut, usually within two days of ordering.

news-hoshi-card-refund-4.text: Alterations to clothes bought at the shop remain free, as long as you bring the receipt.

news-hoshi-card-refund-5.text: Turning to the city, if you're leaving Japan for good, you may be able to get back some of the money on your transit card.

news-hoshi-card-refund-6.text: Return the card at a station office, and you'll receive the five-hundred-yen deposit along with whatever balance is left.

news-hoshi-card-refund-7.text: There's a small handling fee, though it comes out of the balance rather than the deposit, so a nearly empty card costs nothing to return.

news-hoshi-card-refund-8.text: Visitors on a short trip, on the other hand, may prefer to keep the card, since it stays valid as long as it's used once every ten years.

news-hoshi-compost-1.text: Good morning. Resident Services is launching a pilot program this spring that separates food scraps from the regular trash.

news-hoshi-compost-2.text: Households that opt in will receive a small compost bin, with pickups on Tuesdays in place of one of the usual trash days.

news-hoshi-compost-3.text: Those who'd rather not take part can stick with the current schedule; nothing changes unless you sign up.

news-hoshi-compost-4.text: The scheme will be reviewed after three months, and if fewer than a third of homes join, it may be quietly dropped.

news-hoshi-compost-5.text: Meanwhile, with new students and workers settling into Tokyo, carriers are heavily promoting what they call one-yen smartphones.

news-hoshi-compost-6.text: Consumer advisers caution that the headline price usually hinges on returning the handset after two years, in good condition.

news-hoshi-compost-7.text: Keep the phone, or hand it back with a cracked screen, and the remaining installments, often well over fifty thousand yen, come due.

news-hoshi-compost-8.text: In other words, it's less a purchase than a rental, which may suit some people but is rarely spelled out at the counter.

news-hoshi-flight-shift-1.text: Good morning, everyone. Starting with travel, Dodo Airlines has confirmed that its winter timetable takes effect at the end of the month.

news-hoshi-flight-shift-2.text: The two afternoon flights to the mainland will be merged into a single departure at three-forty, a change the airline attributes to a shortage of pilots.

news-hoshi-flight-shift-3.text: Passengers booked on the earlier flight will be moved automatically, while those on the later one can switch for free or request a full refund.

news-hoshi-flight-shift-4.text: Either way, travelers are asked to confirm by Friday, after which the standard change fees kick back in.

news-hoshi-flight-shift-5.text: Turning to the city, with the autumn leaves drawing crowds to places like Nikko and Hakone, booking sites are seeing a surge in last-minute cancellations.

news-hoshi-flight-shift-6.text: Consumer groups point out that free cancellation rarely means what it sounds like, since the deadline is often several days before arrival.

news-hoshi-flight-shift-7.text: What's more, it's usually set in the hotel's local time, which can trip up travelers booking from overseas.

news-hoshi-flight-shift-8.text: And the cheapest rates are typically nonrefundable, so saving a few thousand yen can end up costing you the whole stay.

news-hoshi-heat-aid-1.text: Good morning. With the cold snap expected to linger into next week, the island council has reopened its heating assistance program.

news-hoshi-heat-aid-2.text: Residents over sixty-five qualify automatically and don't need to do anything; the credit will simply appear on their next bill.

news-hoshi-heat-aid-3.text: Everyone else has to apply in person by the fifteenth and bring proof of income, since the program is means-tested.

news-hoshi-heat-aid-4.text: Late applications won't be turned away, but they'll only be processed once the first round of payments has gone out.

news-hoshi-heat-aid-5.text: Turning to the city, the end of the year is the deadline for furusato nozei, the hometown tax donation program.

news-hoshi-heat-aid-6.text: Donations made by December thirty-first count toward this year's taxes, and many residents leave it until the final week.

news-hoshi-heat-aid-7.text: If you give to five or fewer towns and don't otherwise file a tax return, a simple form sent to each town takes care of the deduction.

news-hoshi-heat-aid-8.text: Go over that limit, though, and you'll need to file a return yourself, a step that a surprising number of first-timers overlook.

news-hoshi-marathon-1.text: Good morning. The island council holds its annual emergency drill on Saturday, and this year, the exact time won't be announced in advance.

news-hoshi-marathon-2.text: Sirens will sound at some point between nine and noon, at which point residents are asked to make their way to the plaza.

news-hoshi-marathon-3.text: Taking part is voluntary, but households that do will be first in line for the new emergency kits being handed out afterward.

news-hoshi-marathon-4.text: Anyone who'd rather sit it out is asked to let Resident Services know, so that nobody wastes time searching for them.

news-hoshi-marathon-5.text: Meanwhile, entries for next spring's Tokyo Marathon open this week, and if past years are any guide, the odds of getting in are long.

news-hoshi-marathon-6.text: Typically, only about one applicant in ten is drawn in the general lottery.

news-hoshi-marathon-7.text: Runners who'd rather not leave it to chance can secure a charity spot instead, provided they donate at least a hundred thousand yen.

news-hoshi-marathon-8.text: Charity places are capped, though, and tend to go within days, so anyone on the fence shouldn't wait too long.

news-hoshi-museum-wing-1.text: Good morning. This is Isabelle, and we'll start at the museum, where the long-awaited renovation of the east wing finally gets underway on Monday.

news-hoshi-museum-wing-2.text: The work will be phased, so rather than shutting the museum outright, Blathers will close one gallery at a time over roughly six weeks.

news-hoshi-museum-wing-3.text: The fossil hall is first in line, which means the insect and fish galleries stay open throughout, at least for now.

news-hoshi-museum-wing-4.text: New donations are still welcome at the front desk, though Blathers asks that anything bulky be held back until the work wraps up.

news-hoshi-museum-wing-5.text: Meanwhile, several Tokyo wards are expanding a pilot program that lets commuters rent bicycles by the month rather than by the ride.

news-hoshi-museum-wing-6.text: Officials say the monthly plan works out cheaper for anyone riding more than about four times a week.

news-hoshi-museum-wing-7.text: That said, it only covers the first thirty minutes of each ride, and anything longer is still charged by the minute, a detail that's tripped up a few early users.

news-hoshi-museum-wing-8.text: Sign-ups are handled through the ward's app, and the plan renews automatically unless you cancel before the first of the month.

news-hoshi-pier-plan-1.text: Good morning. The council has unveiled plans for a second pier on the east beach, and it wants to hear from residents before anything is decided.

news-hoshi-pier-plan-2.text: Feedback forms are available at Resident Services until the end of the month, though the council stresses the survey is advisory, not a binding vote.

news-hoshi-pier-plan-3.text: Supporters say the pier would ease congestion at the dock, while some neighbors on the east side worry about noise from early morning boats.

news-hoshi-pier-plan-4.text: Turning to the city, a reminder for anyone taking the bullet train with large luggage: bags over a certain size now need a reservation.

news-hoshi-pier-plan-5.text: If the length, width and height of your bag add up to more than a hundred and sixty centimeters, you'll need a seat with an oversized baggage area.

news-hoshi-pier-plan-6.text: Board without one, and you'll be charged a thousand yen on the train, assuming there's even space to store the bag.

news-hoshi-pier-plan-7.text: Baby strollers are exempt, but nothing over two hundred and fifty centimeters can be brought on at all.

news-hoshi-power-plan-1.text: Good morning, everyone. While the plaza is being resurfaced, the weekly market will move to the dock, starting this Saturday.

news-hoshi-power-plan-2.text: Most stalls are coming along, with the exception of the fish counter, whose freezers can't run on the dock's power supply.

news-hoshi-power-plan-3.text: C.J. will sell straight from his boat instead, but only until his catch runs out, which on a good day is around ten in the morning.

news-hoshi-power-plan-4.text: Otherwise, the market keeps its usual hours, from seven until one.

news-hoshi-power-plan-5.text: Meanwhile, more Tokyo households are being offered electricity plans that charge different rates depending on the time of day.

news-hoshi-power-plan-6.text: Power used late at night can cost roughly a third less, which sounds like a bargain, particularly if you run the washer or charge a car overnight.

news-hoshi-power-plan-7.text: The trade-off is that afternoon rates, especially on hot summer days, can be considerably higher than on a standard plan.

news-hoshi-power-plan-8.text: So for anyone who works from home with the air conditioner running, switching could end up costing more, not less.

news-hoshi-rent-notice-1.text: Good morning. Tom Nook's office has announced that the spring home upgrades, originally slated for April, have been pushed back a month.

news-hoshi-rent-notice-2.text: Residents who've already paid will have their deposits refunded only if they cancel by the end of this week.

news-hoshi-rent-notice-3.text: Those who keep their booking will get a prorated discount instead, reflecting the delay.

news-hoshi-rent-notice-4.text: The office attributes the holdup to a shortage of lumber, which, it says, should ease once the ferry deliveries resume.

news-hoshi-rent-notice-5.text: Meanwhile, as moving season peaks in Tokyo, housing advisers are urging renters to read the fine print on so-called free-rent offers.

news-hoshi-rent-notice-6.text: Many come with a penalty for leaving within two years, which can easily wipe out whatever you saved up front.

news-hoshi-rent-notice-7.text: So, a deal that looks generous on paper may not be one, depending on how long you plan to stay.

news-hoshi-rent-notice-8.text: Advisers also suggest asking whether the key money and cleaning fee are included, since those are rarely mentioned in the listing.

news-hoshi-ski-bus-1.text: Good morning, everyone. After last night's heavy snowfall, Resident Services is asking everyone to clear the path in front of their own home by noon.

news-hoshi-ski-bus-2.text: Residents who can't manage it themselves can request help, although requests will be handled in order of need rather than in the order they come in.

news-hoshi-ski-bus-3.text: The main road to the airfield has already been plowed, but the hill path remains closed until further notice.

news-hoshi-ski-bus-4.text: Turning to the city, ski season is in full swing, and overnight bus tours from Shinjuku to the slopes are booking up fast.

news-hoshi-ski-bus-5.text: Most packages bundle the bus, a lift pass and sometimes rentals, which can work out far cheaper than arranging each piece separately.

news-hoshi-ski-bus-6.text: The catch lies in the cancellation terms: fees typically climb steeply in the final week, reaching half the price the day before departure.

news-hoshi-ski-bus-7.text: And while the operator will refund you in full if it calls off the trip, a lack of snow on the mountain doesn't usually count.

news-hoshi-water-rates-1.text: Good morning, everyone. With the dry spell dragging on, the island council has approved a temporary ordinance on water use.

news-hoshi-water-rates-2.text: Watering gardens is restricted to before eight in the morning and after six at night, except at the community farm, which runs on rainwater.

news-hoshi-water-rates-3.text: In other words, nobody's being told to stop, just to shift their watering to the cooler hours.

news-hoshi-water-rates-4.text: The council will review the measure in two weeks, and it could be lifted sooner if the forecast rain actually materializes.

news-hoshi-water-rates-5.text: Turning to the city, if you're traveling abroad this summer, it's worth taking a closer look at your phone plan before you leave.

news-hoshi-water-rates-6.text: Several carriers have switched to daily roaming passes, which are billed only on days you actually use data.

news-hoshi-water-rates-7.text: The catch is that a single background app update can count as use, so travelers are advised to turn off automatic updates first.

news-hoshi-water-rates-8.text: Otherwise, a trip you'd budgeted for carefully could come with a surprisingly hefty bill once you're back home.

news-kawa-anniversary-1.text: Good morning. Isabelle here, and June means wedding season on the island.

news-kawa-anniversary-2.text: Reese and Cyrus are setting up photo shoots for their anniversary, and they need helpers.

news-kawa-anniversary-3.text: If you sign up, you'll help them set up chairs, flowers and lights on Harvey's island.

news-kawa-anniversary-4.text: The shoots run every evening this month, from six until about eight, so come after dinner if you can.

news-kawa-anniversary-5.text: Turning to the city, the rainy season is here, and that means mold in many homes.

news-kawa-anniversary-6.text: Mold grows fast when the air stays warm and wet, especially in bathrooms and closets.

news-kawa-anniversary-7.text: Experts suggest opening the windows when the rain stops, even for ten minutes.

news-kawa-anniversary-8.text: And leave your closet doors open a little, so air can move around your clothes.

news-kawa-big-dinner-1.text: Good morning, everyone. It's Isabelle, and the plaza already smells wonderful.

news-kawa-big-dinner-2.text: Franklin is cooking his big autumn dinner on Thursday, and he can't do it alone.

news-kawa-big-dinner-3.text: He has run out of a few things, so he's asking everyone to help.

news-kawa-big-dinner-4.text: If you drop off a vegetable or some fish, he'll give you a little gift in return.

news-kawa-big-dinner-5.text: Dinner is ready at six, and everyone is welcome to come and eat.

news-kawa-big-dinner-6.text: Turning to the city, the leaves are turning red and gold in many Tokyo gardens.

news-kawa-big-dinner-7.text: Some gardens, like Rikugien in Komagome, stay open into the evening and light up the trees.

news-kawa-big-dinner-8.text: Lines get long after dark, so try to arrive just before the lights come on.

news-kawa-big-dinner-9.text: And bring a warm jacket, because it gets cold quickly once the sun goes down.

news-kawa-bug-off-1.text: Good morning, everyone. It's Saturday, and it's a big day for bug lovers.

news-kawa-bug-off-2.text: Flick and C.J. are holding the summer bug-off, and it starts this morning at nine.

news-kawa-bug-off-3.text: You'll have four hours to catch as many bugs as you can, so bring a good net.

news-kawa-bug-off-4.text: The judges look at size, so one big beetle can beat a bag of small ones.

news-kawa-bug-off-5.text: Prizes will be handed out in the plaza when it wraps up at one.

news-kawa-bug-off-6.text: Turning to the city, summer is when beer gardens open on the roofs of department stores.

news-kawa-bug-off-7.text: Many of them charge one price for a set time, often around two hours.

news-kawa-bug-off-8.text: Food and drinks are usually included, so you can try a little of everything.

news-kawa-bug-off-9.text: Popular places fill up on Friday nights, so book ahead if you're going with a group.

news-kawa-festivale-1.text: Good morning, island, and get your dancing shoes ready.

news-kawa-festivale-2.text: Pavé is back for Festivale this Sunday, and the parade starts in the plaza at noon.

news-kawa-festivale-3.text: Before then, he's asking everyone to look for colorful feathers on the beach.

news-kawa-festivale-4.text: If you find red, blue or gold ones, you can trade them with him for prizes.

news-kawa-festivale-5.text: Pavé loves to dance, so don't be shy about joining in.

news-kawa-festivale-6.text: Turning to the city, the New Year brings lucky bags, or fukubukuro, to many Tokyo stores.

news-kawa-festivale-7.text: You pay one price, and the bag is filled with things that are worth more.

news-kawa-festivale-8.text: Some stores now show you what's inside, but many still keep it a surprise.

news-kawa-festivale-9.text: The popular ones sell out in the first days of January, so people often line up before the doors open.

news-kawa-first-aid-1.text: Good morning. I'm Isabelle, and I'd like to start with something that could save a life.

news-kawa-first-aid-2.text: Resident services will hold a free first-aid class on Wednesday afternoon, from two until four.

news-kawa-first-aid-3.text: You'll learn what to do if someone falls, gets a bad cut, or stops breathing.

news-kawa-first-aid-4.text: There are only twelve places, so sign up soon if you want to go.

news-kawa-first-aid-5.text: Turning to the city, many people head out on New Year's Eve to visit shrines and temples.

news-kawa-first-aid-6.text: Some train lines run extra trains late into the night, so people can get home after midnight.

news-kawa-first-aid-7.text: But not every line does this, and some stations get very crowded.

news-kawa-first-aid-8.text: So check your line before you go, and pick a meeting place in case you get separated.

news-kawa-hiking-club-1.text: Good morning, and happy Sunday. Let's start with something for those who like to walk.

news-kawa-hiking-club-2.text: The island hiking club is walking up to the top of the hill next Saturday.

news-kawa-hiking-club-3.text: They'll meet at the river bridge at eight-fifteen and come back down around noon.

news-kawa-hiking-club-4.text: New members are welcome, but wear good shoes, because the path gets steep near the top.

news-kawa-hiking-club-5.text: Turning to the city, if your passport runs out soon, you may not have to wait in line.

news-kawa-hiking-club-6.text: In many cases, you can now renew it online and pick it up at the passport office later.

news-kawa-hiking-club-7.text: You'll need a photo taken on your phone and your My Number card.

news-kawa-hiking-club-8.text: The new passport usually takes a week or two, so don't leave it to the last minute.

news-kawa-lighthouse-1.text: Good morning, and thanks for listening. Here's what's new on the island this week.

news-kawa-lighthouse-2.text: The old lighthouse on the east cliff will be open to visitors on Saturday.

news-kawa-lighthouse-3.text: It used to be closed to the public, but the stairs have now been fixed.

news-kawa-lighthouse-4.text: You can climb to the top from ten to three, and it only takes about ten minutes.

news-kawa-lighthouse-5.text: Turning to the city, if you're flying out with big bags, you don't have to drag them onto the train.

news-kawa-lighthouse-6.text: Many convenience stores and hotels can send your suitcase straight to the airport.

news-kawa-lighthouse-7.text: Drop it off at least two days before your flight, and pick it up at a counter there.

news-kawa-lighthouse-8.text: It costs a few thousand yen a bag, which can be worth it on a crowded train.

news-kawa-loop-bus-1.text: Good morning, and happy Monday. I'm Isabelle, with a few changes you'll want to hear about.

news-kawa-loop-bus-2.text: This spring, the island loop bus is adding a stop at the north beach.

news-kawa-loop-bus-3.text: The bus used to come every thirty minutes, but it will now come every twenty.

news-kawa-loop-bus-4.text: You can still pay with a bus card, and you can pick one up at the town hall for free.

news-kawa-loop-bus-5.text: Turning to the city, the long holidays at the start of May are coming up fast.

news-kawa-loop-bus-6.text: If you're planning to take the shinkansen, reserved seats can be gone weeks ahead.

news-kawa-loop-bus-7.text: Seats usually go on sale one month before the travel date, at ten in the morning.

news-kawa-loop-bus-8.text: If you miss out, the non-reserved cars are an option, but be ready to stand for a while.

news-kawa-lost-dog-1.text: Good morning. I'm Isabelle, and we have a small favor to ask today.

news-kawa-lost-dog-2.text: Bunnie's little brown dog, Cookie, ran off near the river last night.

news-kawa-lost-dog-3.text: He's wearing a red collar with his name on it.

news-kawa-lost-dog-4.text: He's friendly, but loud noises scare him, so please don't chase him.

news-kawa-lost-dog-5.text: If you see him, call the town hall, or leave out some water and wait quietly.

news-kawa-lost-dog-6.text: Turning to the city, many Tokyo wards don't allow smoking while you walk down the street.

news-kawa-lost-dog-7.text: Instead, smokers need to find a smoking area, which is often near a station.

news-kawa-lost-dog-8.text: In some wards, people who break the rule can be fined a few thousand yen.

news-kawa-lost-dog-9.text: Most restaurants are smoke-free inside now, too, so look for a sign if you need to know.

news-kawa-photo-studio-1.text: Good morning, island. Isabelle here, and today we have some fun news for you.

news-kawa-photo-studio-2.text: Harvey is opening a small photo studio next to the tailor's shop on Friday.

news-kawa-photo-studio-3.text: You can dress up, pick a background, and take pictures with your friends or family.

news-kawa-photo-studio-4.text: Sessions are free in the first week, but you need to sign up by Thursday at the town hall.

news-kawa-photo-studio-5.text: Turning to the city, many shoppers still forget their bags when they run out for groceries.

news-kawa-photo-studio-6.text: Most stores charge a few yen for each plastic bag at the register.

news-kawa-photo-studio-7.text: That doesn't sound like much, but it adds up if you shop every day.

news-kawa-photo-studio-8.text: So keep a folding bag in your coat pocket, and you won't get caught without one.

news-kawa-recycle-hours-1.text: Good morning, everyone, and happy Wednesday. Here's what's going on around the island.

news-kawa-recycle-hours-2.text: Starting next week, the recycling center by the dock is changing its hours.

news-kawa-recycle-hours-3.text: It used to close at five, but it will now stay open until seven on weekdays.

news-kawa-recycle-hours-4.text: So if you have old cans or big boxes, you can drop them off on your way home from work.

news-kawa-recycle-hours-5.text: Turning to the city, a few train lines are carrying out track work this weekend.

news-kawa-recycle-hours-6.text: On Saturday night, some trains will stop running about an hour earlier than usual.

news-kawa-recycle-hours-7.text: Buses will fill in on the closed section, but they take quite a bit longer.

news-kawa-recycle-hours-8.text: So if you're heading out to dinner, check the last train before you go.

news-kawa-stretches-1.text: Good morning, island. If you're up early, this one's for you.

news-kawa-stretches-2.text: The morning stretches in the plaza are moving to an earlier time next week.

news-kawa-stretches-3.text: They used to start at seven-thirty, but they will now start at six forty-five.

news-kawa-stretches-4.text: That way, more people can join in before they go to work.

news-kawa-stretches-5.text: Bring a mat or a towel, because the grass can be wet in the morning.

news-kawa-stretches-6.text: Turning to the city, more and more people in Tokyo use coin laundries for big things.

news-kawa-stretches-7.text: Many machines are large enough to wash a whole futon or a heavy blanket.

news-kawa-stretches-8.text: A wash and dry usually takes about an hour, so bring something to read.

news-kawa-stretches-9.text: Some shops also let you check on your phone when your load is done.

news-knit-class-1.text: Good morning, island. Here's a look at the day ahead.

news-knit-class-2.text: First up, the town hall is hosting a knitting workshop this weekend, and beginners are especially welcome.

news-knit-class-3.text: The workshop has twelve seats, and eight are already taken, so only four are left.

news-knit-class-4.text: Yarn and needles are provided, and everyone will go home with a scarf, or at least half of one.

news-knit-class-5.text: Turning to the city, heating bills tend to climb in winter, and Tokyo officials have a few tips to keep them down.

news-knit-class-6.text: Close your curtains in the early evening to hold in heat, and set the heater a degree or two lower.

news-knit-class-7.text: Officials also suggest heating the room you're in, not the whole home, and dressing in layers.

news-library-hours-1.text: Good morning, everyone. I'm Isabelle, and here's what's new on the island.

news-library-hours-2.text: First up, the library is extending its evening hours and will now stay open until nine instead of six.

news-library-hours-3.text: The librarian says many residents asked for more time to study after work.

news-library-hours-4.text: The quiet room upstairs is open to everyone, though snacks and drinks are still not allowed.

news-library-hours-5.text: Turning to Tokyo, ward officials are reminding residents to keep an earthquake kit ready at home.

news-library-hours-6.text: A good kit includes water, food that keeps, a flashlight, and enough for at least three days.

news-library-hours-7.text: Experts suggest checking expiration dates once or twice a year and replacing anything old.

news-library-hours-8.text: And make sure everyone at home knows where your nearest evacuation site is.

news-moon-night-1.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the morning news from the island.

news-moon-night-2.text: First up, the island's moon-viewing night is slated for later this week on the hill behind the town hall.

news-moon-night-3.text: The café will serve warm tea from seven, and the viewing itself begins half an hour later, at seven-thirty.

news-moon-night-4.text: Residents are welcome to bring rice dumplings to share with their neighbors.

news-moon-night-5.text: Turning to the city, autumn is when many Tokyo households swap their summer clothes for warmer ones.

news-moon-night-6.text: Before packing summer clothes away, experts suggest washing them first, since even light stains can set over the months.

news-moon-night-7.text: In small apartments, vacuum storage bags can save space, and a moisture absorber helps keep closets dry.

news-moon-night-8.text: And don't rush; on warm afternoons, you may still want a short-sleeved shirt.

news-mori-boat-tours-1.text: Good morning. Kapp'n asked me to pass along some news, so let's start there.

news-mori-boat-tours-2.text: His boat tours, which used to run only on weekends, will now run every day through August.

news-mori-boat-tours-3.text: Tours leave the dock at ten and at two, and each one visits a different small island.

news-mori-boat-tours-4.text: He says the morning boat tends to fill up first, since the sea is calmer then.

news-mori-boat-tours-5.text: And Kapp'n says he'll sing on the way, whether you ask him to or not.

news-mori-boat-tours-6.text: Over in the city, travelers heading to Narita or Haneda have another option besides the train.

news-mori-boat-tours-7.text: Airport limousine buses pick up at many large hotels and stations, and you can stay in your seat the whole way.

news-mori-boat-tours-8.text: They can get stuck in traffic, though, so leave plenty of time when you're catching a flight.

news-mori-boat-tours-9.text: One correction: I said the boat tours leave at two, but the afternoon boat actually leaves at three.

news-mori-bulb-sale-1.text: Good morning. I'm Isabelle, and gardeners, this one's for you.

news-mori-bulb-sale-2.text: Leif is holding a sale on spring flower bulbs, which need to go in the ground before the first frost, so now's the time.

news-mori-bulb-sale-3.text: He says tulips are the most popular this year, and he expects them to sell out within a few days.

news-mori-bulb-sale-4.text: Anyone who isn't sure how deep to plant them can just ask, and he'll gladly show you.

news-mori-bulb-sale-5.text: Over in the city, people heading out for autumn hikes near Tokyo are getting a heads-up about bears.

news-mori-bulb-sale-6.text: Bears have been spotted near trails in the mountains west of the city, including parts of Okutama.

news-mori-bulb-sale-7.text: Officials say hikers should wear a bell, stay on the trail, and avoid walking alone early or late in the day.

news-mori-bulb-sale-8.text: And if you do see a bear, back away slowly, and never run or turn your back on it.

news-mori-countdown-1.text: Good morning. I'm Isabelle, and there are only a few days left in the year.

news-mori-countdown-2.text: The New Year's countdown will be held in the plaza on the thirty-first, starting at eleven at night.

news-mori-countdown-3.text: Organizers say there'll be hot drinks, a short speech from Tom Nook, and fireworks at midnight.

news-mori-countdown-4.text: If you'd rather stay warm at home, the whole thing will also be on the island radio.

news-mori-countdown-5.text: Over in Tokyo, millions of people visit shrines in the first days of January, for what's called hatsumode.

news-mori-countdown-6.text: At big shrines like Meiji Jingu, the lines can be so long that it takes an hour just to reach the front.

news-mori-countdown-7.text: Going on the fourth or fifth, when the crowds have thinned out, is a lot more relaxing, and it counts just the same.

news-mori-countdown-8.text: And if you're going by train, expect the stations near the big shrines to be crowded, too.

news-mori-dive-lessons-1.text: Good morning, everyone. It's Isabelle, and summer on the island means it's time to get in the water.

news-mori-dive-lessons-2.text: Pascal, who knows the sea around here better than anyone, is offering free diving lessons at the south beach.

news-mori-dive-lessons-3.text: Each lesson lasts forty-five minutes, and you'll learn how to find scallops and sea stars safely.

news-mori-dive-lessons-4.text: Wetsuits are provided, but he asks that you bring your own snorkel if you have one, since he only has a few.

news-mori-dive-lessons-5.text: Over in Tokyo, the Obon holidays in mid-August are one of the busiest travel times of the year.

news-mori-dive-lessons-6.text: Trains and highways out of the city get packed, and airfares tend to jump as the dates get closer.

news-mori-dive-lessons-7.text: Travel experts say that leaving a day early, or coming back a day late, can save you money and stress.

news-mori-dive-lessons-8.text: Quick correction to something I said earlier: Pascal's lessons last thirty-five minutes, not forty-five.

news-mori-foot-bath-1.text: Good morning, everyone. It's Isabelle, with something to warm you up on these cold mornings.

news-mori-foot-bath-2.text: A small foot bath has opened next to the museum, and it's already a hit with residents.

news-mori-foot-bath-3.text: It's free and open from noon until nine, and you can borrow a towel from the stand beside it.

news-mori-foot-bath-4.text: The resident who came up with the idea says she just wanted somewhere warm to sit and chat on winter evenings.

news-mori-foot-bath-5.text: Over in Tokyo, if you're clearing out your closet before the New Year, don't just throw old clothes away.

news-mori-foot-bath-6.text: Many clothing stores now have collection boxes, where you can drop off clothes you no longer wear.

news-mori-foot-bath-7.text: Some even give you a discount coupon in return, though it's usually only good at that store, and only for a limited time.

news-mori-foot-bath-8.text: I misspoke earlier: the foot bath closes at eight, not nine. My apologies.

news-mori-fun-run-1.text: Good morning, island. If you've been looking for a reason to get moving, here it is.

news-mori-fun-run-2.text: The autumn fun run, which goes all the way around the island, is set for Sunday morning.

news-mori-fun-run-3.text: There's a five-kilometer course for most people, and a shorter one for kids or anyone who'd rather walk.

news-mori-fun-run-4.text: Runners are asked to check in at the plaza by eight, when the course briefing begins.

news-mori-fun-run-5.text: Over in Tokyo, if your driver's license is up for renewal, you may want to avoid the busiest days.

news-mori-fun-run-6.text: Big licensing centers, like the one in Samezu, tend to be packed on weekends, and the wait can stretch to a couple of hours.

news-mori-fun-run-7.text: Officials suggest going on a weekday morning, and bringing the reminder postcard that came in the mail.

news-mori-fun-run-8.text: And one correction: check-in for the fun run is at seven-thirty, not eight. Please don't be late!

news-mori-radio-hour-1.text: Good morning. I'm Isabelle, and I have news for anyone who's ever wanted to be on the radio.

news-mori-radio-hour-2.text: K.K. is starting a call-in hour on Friday nights, when residents can phone in and request a song.

news-mori-radio-hour-3.text: He says he'll take questions, too, as long as they're not about how old he is.

news-mori-radio-hour-4.text: Lines open at nine, and he warns that the first few nights will probably be busy.

news-mori-radio-hour-5.text: If you miss the show, K.K. says he'll play the best calls again on Sunday afternoon.

news-mori-radio-hour-6.text: Over in the city, food delivery apps have become part of daily life for a lot of people.

news-mori-radio-hour-7.text: But the price you see on the menu isn't always the price you end up paying.

news-mori-radio-hour-8.text: Delivery and service fees can add several hundred yen, and some restaurants charge more on the app than in the shop.

news-mori-radio-hour-9.text: So if you're ordering for one, it's often cheaper to go and pick it up yourself.

news-mori-repair-cafe-1.text: Good morning. It's Isabelle, and I have some news that I think a lot of you will like.

news-mori-repair-cafe-2.text: Cyrano, who has been fixing umbrellas at his shop for years, is starting a free repair afternoon at the town hall.

news-mori-repair-cafe-3.text: Anyone who has a broken chair, lamp or bike can bring it along, and volunteers will try to fix it on the spot.

news-mori-repair-cafe-4.text: It runs on the first Sunday of every month, from one to four.

news-mori-repair-cafe-5.text: Over in Tokyo, a growing number of shops are tightening their return policies, which has caught some shoppers off guard.

news-mori-repair-cafe-6.text: Many now offer store credit instead of cash, especially on sale items that have been opened.

news-mori-repair-cafe-7.text: So hang on to your receipt, and ask about the policy before you pay, not after.

news-mori-repair-cafe-8.text: One correction before we go: the repair afternoon is on the first Saturday of the month, not Sunday. Sorry about that!

news-mori-shop-help-1.text: Good morning, island, and a happy spring to all of you.

news-mori-shop-help-2.text: Timmy and Tommy, who run Nook's Cranny, say they're looking for part-time help on weekends.

news-mori-shop-help-3.text: The job involves stocking shelves and helping customers, and no experience is needed.

news-mori-shop-help-4.text: Anyone who's interested can stop by the shop and fill out a short form before Friday.

news-mori-shop-help-5.text: Timmy says the pay is fair, and Tommy says the snacks in the back room are even better.

news-mori-shop-help-6.text: Over in Tokyo, April is a busy month at ticket machines, as people buy passes for school or work.

news-mori-shop-help-7.text: A commuter pass lets you ride as often as you like between two stations, which usually works out much cheaper.

news-mori-shop-help-8.text: You can buy one at most station machines, or on your phone if you use a mobile card.

news-mori-shop-help-9.text: One last thing: Timmy and Tommy need those forms by Wednesday, not Friday. Sorry about that.

news-mori-stamp-rally-1.text: Good morning, everyone. Isabelle here, and spring brings back one of my favorite events.

news-mori-stamp-rally-2.text: The stamp rally, which takes you to six spots around the island, starts this weekend.

news-mori-stamp-rally-3.text: Pick up a card at the town hall, collect a stamp at each spot, and bring it back for a prize.

news-mori-stamp-rally-4.text: Organizers say last year's prizes ran out by Sunday afternoon, so it pays to go early.

news-mori-stamp-rally-5.text: Cards are free, and you have until the end of the month to finish.

news-mori-stamp-rally-6.text: Over in Tokyo, a lot of shops are pushing cashless payments by offering points on every purchase.

news-mori-stamp-rally-7.text: Several wards have run campaigns where paying by phone at local shops earns extra points.

news-mori-stamp-rally-8.text: The catch is that most of these campaigns have a monthly limit, and the points stop once you hit it.

news-mori-stamp-rally-9.text: Quick fix to something I said earlier: the stamp rally has eight spots this year, not six.

news-mori-travel-talk-1.text: Good morning, everyone. Let me start with an event for anyone who has itchy feet.

news-mori-travel-talk-2.text: Gulliver, who has washed up on our beach more times than anyone can count, is giving a travel talk tonight.

news-mori-travel-talk-3.text: He'll share stories from his trips and tips on packing light, which, he admits, he's still learning himself.

news-mori-travel-talk-4.text: The talk starts at seven at the museum, and seats are first come, first served.

news-mori-travel-talk-5.text: Over in Tokyo, where many people live in small apartments, noise is one of the most common problems between neighbors.

news-mori-travel-talk-6.text: Running a washing machine or a vacuum late at night is a frequent cause, since the sound carries through the floors.

news-mori-travel-talk-7.text: Many buildings have house rules about this, so it's worth reading yours if you've just moved in.

news-mori-travel-talk-8.text: And if a neighbor does knock on your door, a quick apology and a quieter schedule usually go a long way.

news-mori-tune-vote-1.text: Good morning, island. Today's top story is one you actually get a say in.

news-mori-tune-vote-2.text: The town hall is asking residents to vote on a new town tune, the one that plays every hour in the plaza.

news-mori-tune-vote-3.text: There are three tunes to choose from, and you can listen to each one at the front desk before you decide.

news-mori-tune-vote-4.text: Voting closes on Thursday, and the winning tune will start playing next month.

news-mori-tune-vote-5.text: Over in Tokyo, more restaurants are charging a fee to customers who book a table and don't show up.

news-mori-tune-vote-6.text: Some ask for a card number when you reserve, so the fee can be charged automatically.

news-mori-tune-vote-7.text: Owners say no-shows hurt them the most with set courses, which are prepared ahead of time and can't be sold to anyone else.

news-mori-tune-vote-8.text: One correction before we go: voting on the town tune closes on Tuesday, not Thursday. Sorry for the mix-up.

news-museum-tour-1.text: Good morning, everyone. Here are today's top stories from the island.

news-museum-tour-2.text: First up, the museum is launching free guided tours, led by the curator himself, for groups of up to ten.

news-museum-tour-3.text: Tours start at the main hall and end in the aquarium, and each one runs about an hour.

news-museum-tour-4.text: Sign-up sheets are at the front desk, and the curator asks visitors to keep their voices down near the fossils.

news-museum-tour-5.text: Turning to the city, stations across Tokyo are asking riders to stand still on escalators instead of walking.

news-museum-tour-6.text: Officials say walking up or down can lead to falls, and it's especially risky for older passengers.

news-museum-tour-7.text: Riders are encouraged to hold the handrail, and if you're in a hurry, the stairs are usually close by.

news-mushroom-walk-1.text: Good morning, and happy Tuesday. I'm Isabelle, and here's what's happening on the island.

news-mushroom-walk-2.text: First up, the autumn mushroom walk is back, and this year it will start at the edge of the forest behind the museum.

news-mushroom-walk-3.text: The group leaves at ten sharp; that's a change from the nine o'clock start listed on the poster.

news-mushroom-walk-4.text: Please don't eat anything you find along the way until our resident expert has taken a look.

news-mushroom-walk-5.text: Turning to the city, autumn is when many Tokyo clinics start offering flu shots.

news-mushroom-walk-6.text: Doctors say it takes about two weeks for the vaccine to start working, so it's best not to wait until winter.

news-mushroom-walk-7.text: Some wards help cover the cost for older residents and young children, so check your ward's website.

news-mushroom-walk-8.text: And many clinics require a reservation, so call before you go.

news-music-night-1.text: Good morning, and happy Saturday! Here's what's going on around the island this weekend.

news-music-night-2.text: First up, the plaza hosts a music night this evening, with island residents performing songs they've written themselves.

news-music-night-3.text: There are eleven performers on the list, up from seven last time, so the show will run a bit longer.

news-music-night-4.text: Chairs are limited, and organizers suggest bringing something to sit on.

news-music-night-5.text: Turning to the city, a reminder for Tokyo riders: you can top up your IC card at most station ticket machines.

news-music-night-6.text: Many convenience stores will also add money to your card at the register, which can save time during rush hour.

news-music-night-7.text: If your balance is too low at the gate, don't worry; a fare adjustment machine nearby can fix it.

news-music-night-8.text: And register your card if you can, so it can be replaced if it's lost.

news-new-neighbor-1.text: Good morning, and happy Wednesday. We're halfway through the week, and here's the island news.

news-new-neighbor-2.text: First up, a new resident is moving in this week, and the welcome party at the plaza is set for tomorrow evening.

news-new-neighbor-3.text: The party was first planned for six, but it's been pushed back to seven so more residents can make it.

news-new-neighbor-4.text: Residents are welcome to bring a small gift, like fruit or flowers from their gardens.

news-new-neighbor-5.text: Turning to the city, if you've recently moved within Tokyo, officials remind you that trash rules vary by ward.

news-new-neighbor-6.text: Burnable garbage, plastics, and cans may go out on different days, and some wards collect them early in the morning.

news-new-neighbor-7.text: Putting bags out on the wrong day can leave them uncollected, and neighbors do notice.

news-new-neighbor-8.text: Most wards offer a printed calendar or an app, so check yours.

news-plaza-lights-1.text: Good morning. I'm Isabelle, and here's your island news.

news-plaza-lights-2.text: First up, the winter lights are up in the plaza, and they'll stay lit every evening until the end of the season.

news-plaza-lights-3.text: The lights come on at five and go off at eleven, an hour later than last winter's ten o'clock.

news-plaza-lights-4.text: Residents are asked to keep the noise down near the houses on the north side after dark.

news-plaza-lights-5.text: Turning to the city, Tokyo winters are famously dry, and doctors say dry air helps colds spread.

news-plaza-lights-6.text: They recommend keeping indoor humidity around fifty percent, and a humidifier or even wet towels can help.

news-plaza-lights-7.text: Washing your hands when you get home and gargling are still two of the simplest ways to stay healthy.

news-plaza-sweep-1.text: Good morning, and thanks for tuning in to the island news.

news-plaza-sweep-2.text: First up, the spring plaza cleanup is slated for this weekend, and volunteers are needed to sweep paths and replant flower beds.

news-plaza-sweep-3.text: Volunteers should meet by the fountain at seven-thirty, not at the town hall as first announced.

news-plaza-sweep-4.text: Gloves and trash bags will be handed out, and tea will be served afterward at the café.

news-plaza-sweep-5.text: Turning to the city, as spring brings more cyclists out, many Tokyo wards are cracking down on illegal bike parking.

news-plaza-sweep-6.text: Bikes left near station entrances can be removed and taken to a storage lot, sometimes far from the station.

news-plaza-sweep-7.text: Getting one back usually means a trip to that lot and a fee, so officials suggest using paid parking instead.

news-plaza-sweep-8.text: Check your ward's website for bike parking near your station.

news-pumpkin-show-1.text: Good morning, and thanks for listening. I'm Isabelle.

news-pumpkin-show-2.text: First up, the pumpkin contest returns to the plaza, and growers have until the end of the month to enter.

news-pumpkin-show-3.text: Judging was announced for the morning, but it'll actually take place in the afternoon, at two, so everyone can attend.

news-pumpkin-show-4.text: The heaviest pumpkin wins a ribbon, and smaller ones will be carved into lanterns for the evening.

news-pumpkin-show-5.text: Turning to the city, autumn is sports day season at many Tokyo schools.

news-pumpkin-show-6.text: Neighbors may hear music and loudspeakers early on weekend mornings, and schools usually post a notice in advance.

news-pumpkin-show-7.text: Parents are asked not to save spots with tarps before the gates open, and to leave cars at home.

news-pumpkin-show-8.text: Many schools also ban photos of other people's children, so check the rules first.

news-river-benches-1.text: Good morning, and welcome to another day on the island. I'm Isabelle.

news-river-benches-2.text: First up, six new benches have been placed along the river, along with two picnic tables near the waterfall.

news-river-benches-3.text: Residents donated the wood, and the carpenter who built them says they should last for years.

news-river-benches-4.text: Officials are asking everyone to take their trash with them, since there are no bins along the river yet.

news-river-benches-5.text: Turning to the city, rail officials are reminding Tokyo riders how priority seating works.

news-river-benches-6.text: The seats near the ends of each car are meant for older people, pregnant women, people with disabilities, and those with small children.

news-river-benches-7.text: You can sit there when the train is empty, but offer your seat as soon as someone needs it.

news-river-benches-8.text: And some riders need a seat even if it doesn't show, so look for the badges on bags.

news-snowman-prize-1.text: Good morning, and happy Thursday. Here's what's happening on the island.

news-snowman-prize-2.text: First up, the winter snowman contest is open again, and entries will be judged at the plaza at the end of the month.

news-snowman-prize-3.text: Each household may enter up to two snowmen, not three as in past years, to leave room for everyone.

news-snowman-prize-4.text: Organizers will provide buckets and scarves, and hot cocoa will be waiting at the café afterward.

news-snowman-prize-5.text: Turning to the city, Tokyo fire officials say winter is the season for house fires, many of them started by heaters.
