tachi-ballgame-1.text: So, the Cubs game on Saturday. Are we actually goin', or just watchin' it at the bar?

tachi-ballgame-2.text: Going, obviously. Summer at Wrigley, hot dogs, the seventh-inning stretch. You can't get that on TV.

tachi-ballgame-3.text: You also can't get a seat. The bleachers are sold out, and the good seats are like ninety bucks each.

tachi-ballgame-4.text: Ninety bucks? For that, I'd rather stay in an' order wings.

tachi-ballgame-5.text: Come on. My cousin can get us standing-room tickets for twenty-five.

tachi-ballgame-6.text: Twenty-five? Okay, that changes things. I'm in.

tachi-ballgame-7.text: Standin' for three hours? Pass. But I'll meet you guys after for wings.

tachi-ballgame-8.text: Deal. Gates open at five, so let's meet at the Addison stop at four-thirty.

tachi-bbq-gossip-1.text: Okay, don't look now, but Kenta and Yui just showed up. Together.

tachi-bbq-gossip-2.text: Together together? Or just the same train?

tachi-bbq-gossip-3.text: Same train, obviously. She's been seein' that guy from 'er climbing gym forever.

tachi-bbq-gossip-4.text: Not anymore. They broke up in, like, January.

tachi-bbq-gossip-5.text: Did they? Oh. Well, then, I guess... he did bring 'er a drink without askin' what she wanted.

tachi-bbq-gossip-6.text: That's nothing. I brought you a drink without asking.

tachi-bbq-gossip-7.text: You brought me a warm beer. That's different.

tachi-bbq-gossip-8.text: Shh, they're coming over. Act normal. Someone say something about the weather.

tachi-bootcamp-1.text: So, are we doin' the six a m bootcamp in Yoyogi or not? It's only three thousand a month.

tachi-bootcamp-2.text: I'm so in. I need something to get me out of bed.

tachi-bootcamp-3.text: That sounds really fun. I'll definitely think about it.

tachi-bootcamp-5.text: It's not a no! It's just... six a m. In January. Outside.

tachi-bootcamp-6.text: There's an indoor option on rainy days, an' the first week's free.

tachi-bootcamp-7.text: Free? Well, that's different. Fine, I'll come for the free week and see.

tachi-bootcamp-8.text: Ha! Monday, six sharp. I'll pick ya both up at a quarter to.

tachi-credit-stolen-1.text: So guess whose name was on the slides at the board meeting. Not mine.

tachi-credit-stolen-2.text: No way! Your manager's? After you stayed till ten every night?

tachi-credit-stolen-3.text: Classic. You should email the director. Just, like, casually mention it was yer work.

tachi-credit-stolen-4.text: Hmm, I'd talk to the manager first. Goin' over 'er head could backfire.

tachi-credit-stolen-5.text: Ugh, I hate confrontation. I was just gonna let it go.

tachi-credit-stolen-6.text: If you let it go, she'll do it again. Trust me.

tachi-credit-stolen-7.text: Yeah... you're right. Okay. I'll ask her for a quick chat tomorrow. Not an angry one, just... a chat.

tachi-credit-stolen-8.text: Good for you. An' keep yer old drafts. Just in case.

tachi-deposit-letter-1.text: So the landlord's keepin' nine hundred of our deposit. Professional cleaning, plus significant wall damage.

tachi-deposit-letter-2.text: Significant? It was three nail holes. I've seen bigger damage from a sticky note.

tachi-deposit-letter-3.text: Look, I hate this as much as you do, but fightin' it means small claims court, an' that's months of our lives for, what, three hundred each?

tachi-deposit-letter-4.text: It doesn't hafta go that far. In this state they hafta itemize it within thirty days, with receipts. Did they?

tachi-deposit-letter-5.text: Nope. Jus' an email that said deductions applied. That's it.

tachi-deposit-letter-6.text: Wait, seriously? No receipts at all? Okay, that changes things. If they skipped that, we've actually got a leg ta stand on.

tachi-deposit-letter-7.text: Exactly. So we don't sue anybody. We send one polite, very boring letter citin' the law, an' give 'em two weeks.

tachi-deposit-letter-8.text: Boring I can do. I'll dig up the move-out photos, so they can't say the walls were trashed.

tachi-family-plan-1.text: Okay, my plan's going up to sixty-five a month. I'm switching carriers.

tachi-family-plan-2.text: Why don't we jus' do a family plan? Three lines is like forty each.

tachi-family-plan-3.text: Forty each, plus taxes an' fees. It's never actually forty.

tachi-family-plan-4.text: Even at fifty, I'm still saving fifteen bucks. I'm in.

tachi-family-plan-5.text: My worry is, who's payin' the bill? Las' time we split something, I chased you guys fer three months.

tachi-family-plan-6.text: Okay, that was one time. Fine, autopay. Everyone's share goes out on the firs', automatically.

tachi-family-plan-7.text: Automatically? Okay. If it's automatic, I'm in too. But the account's in my name.

tachi-family-plan-8.text: Deal. I'll port my number over this weekend.

tachi-farewell-dinner-1.text: So, Kenji's going-away dinner. Are we still doing Thursday?

tachi-farewell-dinner-2.text: I'd rather not, to be honest. The client deck's due Friday mornin', an' Thursday night's when it all goes wrong.

tachi-farewell-dinner-3.text: Fair, but it's his last week. He's already off on Friday.

tachi-farewell-dinner-4.text: What about Wednesday? Same place, the Thai one.

tachi-farewell-dinner-6.text: Wednesday's my kid's school thing. I could come late, maybe eight-thirty?

tachi-farewell-dinner-7.text: Then let's do Wednesday, and we'll save you a seat. Better late than never.

tachi-farewell-dinner-8.text: Okay, fine. Wednesday. I'll be the one still wearin' the P T A lanyard.

tachi-film-verdict-1.text: Okay, be honest. What did everyone think?

tachi-film-verdict-2.text: Oh, it was a masterpiece. Three hours, an' I coulda told ya the ending after twenty minutes.

tachi-film-verdict-3.text: Harsh! I thought the ending was the best part. I didn't see the twist comin' at all.

tachi-film-verdict-4.text: I'm with Audie, honestly. The middle dragged. I almost fell asleep.

tachi-film-verdict-5.text: But the twist, though! The sister was the one sending the letters the whole time!

tachi-film-verdict-6.text: Wait, the sister? I thought it was the neighbor.

tachi-film-verdict-8.text: Okay, if it was the sister, that's actually pretty clever. Fine, I take it back. It was good.

tachi-film-verdict-9.text: Okay. Ramen's on me, an' I'll walk ya through it from the start.

tachi-fireworks-rain-1.text: The forecast says a seventy percent chance of rain on Saturday. Are we still goin' to the fireworks?

tachi-fireworks-rain-2.text: Of course we are. They only cancel for a real storm. A little drizzle never stopped anybody.

tachi-fireworks-rain-3.text: Standin' in a wet yukata for two hours with a million people? Can't wait.

tachi-fireworks-rain-4.text: He's got a point. Last year the trains afterward were a nightmare, even when it was dry.

tachi-fireworks-rain-5.text: Okay, how 'bout this. My buddy has an apartment in Asakusa with a balcony. Ya can see the whole thing from there.

tachi-fireworks-rain-6.text: A balcony? With a roof? Okay, I'm in. I'll bring snacks.

tachi-fireworks-rain-7.text: I'll check the official site Saturday morning. If it's called off, we'll just get takeout at 'is buddy's place.

tachi-flight-canceled-1.text: Okay, they canceled the eight-forty. The next flight with seats is tomorrow at six-ten a m, an' they'll comp a hotel.

tachi-flight-canceled-2.text: Six-ten means leavin' the hotel at four-thirty. I have a client at noon, an' I'd rather not show up as a zombie.

tachi-flight-canceled-3.text: Or we rent a car right now an' drive. It's five hours, maybe six. We'd be home by two a m.

tachi-flight-canceled-4.text: In a snowstorm? The pass closed an hour ago. I jus' saw it on the board.

tachi-flight-canceled-5.text: Huh. Didn' know that. Okay, scratch the car. I'm not dyin' on a mountain ta save a hotel night.

tachi-flight-canceled-6.text: Wait, the agent jus' said there's a nine-fifteen tomorrow too, with two seats. Sorry, three. She miscounted.

tachi-flight-canceled-7.text: The nine-fifteen gets in at ten-forty. Can ya make a noon client from the airport?

tachi-flight-canceled-8.text: If I go straight there, yes. Sleep beats bein' early. Book us on the nine-fifteen.

tachi-hama-airport-way-1.text: Our flight is at three forty. Let's leave the hotel by one.

tachi-hama-airport-way-2.text: A taxi costs eight thousand yen. The train is cheaper.

tachi-hama-airport-way-3.text: The bus is cheap too, and it's direct.

tachi-hama-airport-way-5.text: But the bus takes ninety minutes. That's too long.

tachi-hama-airport-way-6.text: The train takes fifty minutes. It's cheap and fast.

tachi-hama-airport-way-7.text: Okay, you're right. Let's take the train.

tachi-hama-airport-way-8.text: Good. Then we leave at one.

tachi-hama-cold-oranges-1.text: Amy has a bad cold. Let's buy her some medicine.

tachi-hama-cold-oranges-2.text: She needs a doctor. Let's take her to one.

tachi-hama-cold-oranges-3.text: But it's Sunday. The clinics are closed today.

tachi-hama-cold-oranges-4.text: Oh, right. Then medicine is fine.

tachi-hama-cold-oranges-5.text: Let's get some oranges too. She loves oranges.

tachi-hama-cold-oranges-6.text: Good idea. The drugstore is open until nine.

tachi-hama-funny-movie-1.text: Let's watch a scary movie tonight.

tachi-hama-funny-movie-2.text: No, thanks. Scary movies give me bad dreams.

tachi-hama-funny-movie-3.text: How about a funny movie? I want to laugh.

tachi-hama-funny-movie-4.text: Okay, okay. A funny movie is fine.

tachi-hama-gift-mug-1.text: It's Ken's birthday on Friday. What should we get him?

tachi-hama-gift-mug-2.text: He likes coffee. Let's buy him a nice mug.

tachi-hama-gift-mug-3.text: He has a lot of mugs. I want to buy a book.

tachi-hama-gift-mug-5.text: Yes. He reads on the train every day.

tachi-hama-gift-mug-6.text: A book is a nice idea.

tachi-hama-gift-mug-7.text: Okay, you're right. No mug. Let's go to the bookstore after lunch.

tachi-hama-lunch-1.text: I'm hungry. Let's have pizza for lunch.

tachi-hama-lunch-2.text: Pizza again? I want sushi today.

tachi-hama-lunch-3.text: I don't eat fish. Can we get curry?

tachi-hama-lunch-5.text: Oh, I forgot. Then let's have curry.

tachi-hama-lunch-6.text: Great. The curry shop is near the station.

tachi-hama-party-rain-1.text: Let's have the party in the park on Saturday.

tachi-hama-party-rain-2.text: It's going to rain on Saturday. Let's have it at my house.

tachi-hama-party-rain-3.text: I can bring some games and a cake.

tachi-hama-party-rain-4.text: Rain? Oh. Then your house is better.

tachi-hama-red-leaves-1.text: Let's go to the beach this weekend.

tachi-hama-red-leaves-2.text: The beach? It's too cold to swim now.

tachi-hama-red-leaves-3.text: Let's go to the mountains. The leaves are red now.

tachi-hama-red-leaves-4.text: Red leaves? I want to see them. Okay, the mountains.

tachi-hama-red-leaves-5.text: Good. I'll check the train times tonight.

tachi-hama-red-leaves-6.text: Let's leave early on Saturday morning.

tachi-hama-soup-night-1.text: What do you want for dinner? I can cook tonight.

tachi-hama-soup-night-2.text: Let's make tacos. I love tacos.

tachi-hama-soup-night-3.text: It's so cold today. I want hot soup.

tachi-hama-soup-night-4.text: Tacos need meat, and we don't have any meat.

tachi-hama-soup-night-5.text: Oh. Then I want soup too.

tachi-hama-soup-night-6.text: Great. I can buy bread at the store.

tachi-hama-station-hotel-1.text: This hotel is near the station. It's twelve thousand yen.

tachi-hama-station-hotel-2.text: That's a lot. This one is only seven thousand yen.

tachi-hama-station-hotel-3.text: But that one is far. It's forty minutes by bus.

tachi-hama-station-hotel-4.text: Forty minutes? That's too far. You're right.

tachi-hama-station-hotel-5.text: And the station hotel has free breakfast.

tachi-hama-window-seat-2.text: Outside is nice, but it's very windy.

tachi-hama-window-seat-3.text: Let's sit inside. I like the window seats.

tachi-hama-window-seat-4.text: Windy? Okay, then let's sit inside.

tachi-hama-window-seat-6.text: Tea for me, please. Not coffee.

tachi-hanami-spot-1.text: So, hanami this Saturday. Meguro River, right? The lanterns are so pretty at night.

tachi-hanami-spot-2.text: Pretty, sure. Also completely packed. You can't sit down there, ya just shuffle along.

tachi-hanami-spot-3.text: That's what I was gonna say. I'd rather have a picnic somewhere. Shinjuku Gyoen?

tachi-hanami-spot-4.text: Gyoen doesn't allow alcohol, though. Just so you know.

tachi-hanami-spot-5.text: Oh, right. Yoyogi, then. Ya can bring whatever ya want.

tachi-hanami-spot-6.text: Hmm. Okay, fine, a picnic does sound nicer. But can we at least walk along the river after? Just for the lanterns?

tachi-hanami-spot-7.text: If we must. I'll bring the blanket.

tachi-hanami-spot-8.text: An' I'll grab drinks. Let's say Yoyogi at one?

tachi-hiring-pick-1.text: Okay, we need a decision on the analyst role by Friday. Priya or Marcus?

tachi-hiring-pick-2.text: Marcus. He's sharp, he's polished, an' honestly, he interviewed like 'e'd already been here a year.

tachi-hiring-pick-3.text: Polished is one word for it. When I asked about the project that tanked, it was somehow everybody's fault but 'is.

tachi-hiring-pick-4.text: Priya was rougher around the edges, but 'er case study was the only one that actually answered the question we asked.

tachi-hiring-pick-5.text: I'm not sayin' she's bad. I'm sayin' Marcus could hit the ground runnin'.

tachi-hiring-pick-6.text: Runnin' where, though? The las' guy who hit the ground runnin' ran straight to a competitor after six months.

tachi-hiring-pick-7.text: ...Okay, fair. That one stung. Fine, I can live with Priya, as long as we pair 'er with a mentor fer the first quarter.

tachi-hiring-pick-8.text: Done. I'll make 'er the offer today, an' you two figure out who's mentorin'.

tachi-hoshi-bad-rental-1.text: Well, the listing did say "cozy." I guess that's what they meant by cozy.

tachi-hoshi-bad-rental-10.text: Not if we book the hotel down the street first. They had rooms an hour ago.

tachi-hoshi-bad-rental-11.text: ...Fine. Book it, and then we'll message the host. In that order.

tachi-hoshi-bad-rental-2.text: Cozy is one word for it. The second bedroom is basically a closet with a window.

tachi-hoshi-bad-rental-3.text: I mean, the location's great, and we're barely going to be here.

tachi-hoshi-bad-rental-4.text: Says the person who got the room with the actual bed.

tachi-hoshi-bad-rental-5.text: Okay, but here's the thing. The photos showed a washer, and there's no washer. That's a misrepresentation.

tachi-hoshi-bad-rental-6.text: Huh. If that's in writing, we could ask for a partial refund, right?

tachi-hoshi-bad-rental-7.text: I'd go further. The policy says we can cancel within twenty-four hours of check-in and get the rest prorated.

tachi-hoshi-bad-rental-9.text: But then we're hunting for a new place at nine p.m. in peak season. That seems like a stretch.

tachi-hoshi-city-pass-1.text: This pass gets us into five museums plus the observation deck for a hundred twenty-nine dollars. That's a steal, right?

tachi-hoshi-city-pass-10.text: ...I hate it when you're both right. Fine. Timed tickets it is.

tachi-hoshi-city-pass-2.text: It's a steal if we actually go to five museums. In three days.

tachi-hoshi-city-pass-3.text: Which, given how long you spent in the first one yesterday, seems a little optimistic.

tachi-hoshi-city-pass-5.text: Realistically, we'll do the Met and the deck. What are those separately?

tachi-hoshi-city-pass-6.text: Thirty for the Met, forty-four for the deck. So seventy-four, give or take.

tachi-hoshi-city-pass-7.text: Okay, but the pass also lets you skip the line, which in July could save us an hour each time.

tachi-hoshi-city-pass-8.text: An hour in line versus fifty-five dollars. I'll take the line and an iced coffee.

tachi-hoshi-city-pass-9.text: Or we book timed tickets online, which gets us in without the line anyway.

tachi-hoshi-coast-road-1.text: If we rent a car, we can stop wherever we want on the way. That's half the fun of a road trip.

tachi-hoshi-coast-road-2.text: It's also six hours each way, and the tolls alone run about twenty thousand yen.

tachi-hoshi-coast-road-3.text: Plus parking in Kanazawa, which, from what I've read, isn't cheap either.

tachi-hoshi-coast-road-5.text: Split three ways, the bullet train's still faster. Two and a half hours, and nobody has to drive.

tachi-hoshi-coast-road-6.text: Okay, but the whole point was the coast road. You can't see the coast from a tunnel.

tachi-hoshi-coast-road-7.text: So take the train up, and rent a car just for the day we do the coast. Best of both worlds.

tachi-hoshi-coast-road-8.text: I could live with that. As long as I'm not the one driving.

tachi-hoshi-coast-road-9.text: Fine, fine. I'll look into one-day rentals near the station. But I'm picking the music.

tachi-hoshi-dog-sitter-1.text: The kennel near us wants six thousand five hundred yen a night, so a week is over forty-five thousand.

tachi-hoshi-dog-sitter-10.text: I'll book someone tonight. And I'm buying a self-watering pot. No offense.

tachi-hoshi-dog-sitter-2.text: I keep telling you, I can just stay at your place. I work from home anyway.

tachi-hoshi-dog-sitter-3.text: That's really generous. It's just that, last time, the plants didn't exactly make it.

tachi-hoshi-dog-sitter-4.text: Those plants were already on their way out.

tachi-hoshi-dog-sitter-5.text: And Biscuit needs two walks a day, one of them before seven. That's a big ask.

tachi-hoshi-dog-sitter-6.text: Before seven? Okay, that part I didn't sign up for.

tachi-hoshi-dog-sitter-7.text: What about the sitter app? Someone comes by for the morning walk, and you take the evenings.

tachi-hoshi-dog-sitter-8.text: That's maybe twenty thousand for the week, all in. Way less than the kennel.

tachi-hoshi-dog-sitter-9.text: Mornings covered, evenings mine. I can work with that.

tachi-hoshi-extend-trip-1.text: So the hotel says we can keep the room through Thursday, at the same rate. I'm just putting that out there.

tachi-hoshi-extend-trip-10.text: It's on their site. Free changes for anyone flying out Tuesday. Okay, I'm calling the hotel back.

tachi-hoshi-extend-trip-11.text: And I'll be calling my dentist. Again.

tachi-hoshi-extend-trip-2.text: Same rate is nice, but our flights are nonrefundable. Changing them isn't exactly free.

tachi-hoshi-extend-trip-3.text: How much is the change fee, out of curiosity?

tachi-hoshi-extend-trip-4.text: A hundred and fifty each, plus whatever the fare difference is. Which, this week, is not nothing.

tachi-hoshi-extend-trip-5.text: Right. For what it's worth, I'm in. I'd just have to move that thing on Wednesday.

tachi-hoshi-extend-trip-6.text: The "thing" being a dentist appointment you've rescheduled three times.

tachi-hoshi-extend-trip-7.text: Four, actually. At this point, what's one more?

tachi-hoshi-extend-trip-8.text: Hang on. If the airline waives the fee for the storm on Tuesday, the math is completely different.

tachi-hoshi-extend-trip-9.text: Is that a real thing, or wishful thinking?

tachi-hoshi-last-train-1.text: Heads-up: the last train's at twelve ten, and it's a fifteen-minute walk to the station.

tachi-hoshi-last-train-10.text: Fine. I'll walk out with you. No point being the last one here.

tachi-hoshi-last-train-2.text: It's barely eleven-thirty. Things are just getting going.

tachi-hoshi-last-train-3.text: Says the guy who lives two stops away. Some of us have a transfer.

tachi-hoshi-last-train-5.text: From here to Kichijoji? That's nine thousand yen, minimum, and that's if we can even find one at one a.m.

tachi-hoshi-last-train-6.text: Which, on a Saturday in Shibuya, is a big if.

tachi-hoshi-last-train-7.text: Okay, but they're about to bring out the cake, and leaving before the cake is just rude.

tachi-hoshi-last-train-8.text: Then we eat the cake fast and go at five to twelve... Actually, no — make it a quarter to. Five to is cutting it way too close.

tachi-hoshi-last-train-9.text: A quarter to it is. I'm setting an alarm, because I know us.

tachi-hoshi-red-eye-1.text: Okay, two options. The red-eye tonight, or the seven a.m. tomorrow and one more night at the airport hotel.

tachi-hoshi-red-eye-11.text: So a hundred and forty each, to not risk a whole day in Denver. ...Book the room before it's gone.

tachi-hoshi-red-eye-2.text: The red-eye's eighty bucks a head cheaper. And we'd save on the hotel, too.

tachi-hoshi-red-eye-3.text: Sure, if you can sleep sitting up. Some of us can't.

tachi-hoshi-red-eye-5.text: The catch is the layover. It's in Denver, and it's only forty minutes.

tachi-hoshi-red-eye-6.text: Forty minutes in Denver in January. What could possibly go wrong?

tachi-hoshi-red-eye-7.text: Okay, that's... tighter than I thought. If we miss it, we're stuck there all day.

tachi-hoshi-red-eye-8.text: Whereas the morning flight is nonstop. We'd land by noon either way.

tachi-hoshi-red-eye-9.text: What does the hotel run us, split three ways?

tachi-hoshi-ridge-storm-1.text: So the forecast says a sixty percent chance of thunderstorms after two. I'd call that a solid maybe.

tachi-hoshi-ridge-storm-10.text: ...Fine. But I'm holding you to the no-arguments part. And I'm packing an actual rain jacket this time.

tachi-hoshi-ridge-storm-2.text: A solid maybe, on a ridge with no shelter. Sounds relaxing.

tachi-hoshi-ridge-storm-3.text: We could start at six instead of nine. We'd be off the ridge by noon, well ahead of it.

tachi-hoshi-ridge-storm-4.text: Six a.m. On my day off.

tachi-hoshi-ridge-storm-5.text: The bigger issue is the bus. The first one up to the trailhead isn't till seven forty.

tachi-hoshi-ridge-storm-6.text: Then we drive. My cousin's car is just sitting there.

tachi-hoshi-ridge-storm-7.text: Your cousin, who still hasn't forgiven you for the dent?

tachi-hoshi-ridge-storm-9.text: Look, if the sky looks iffy by the halfway point, we turn around. No arguments.

tachi-hoshi-ryokan-bath-1.text: So, for our second night, they're offering the room with a private open-air bath, for fourteen thousand yen more. Per person.

tachi-hoshi-ryokan-bath-10.text: Get the nine o'clock, if they've got it.

tachi-hoshi-ryokan-bath-2.text: Per person. For a bath. Which, I'd point out, is what the big shared one downstairs is for.

tachi-hoshi-ryokan-bath-3.text: The shared one's nice, but it's packed after dinner. Last night it was like a train platform in there.

tachi-hoshi-ryokan-bath-4.text: That's the part that gets me.

tachi-hoshi-ryokan-bath-5.text: Apparently you can also book the small family bath. Forty-five minutes, no charge, first come, first served.

tachi-hoshi-ryokan-bath-7.text: Only catch is, the slots go fast. The front desk said the evening ones are usually gone by four.

tachi-hoshi-ryokan-bath-8.text: It's three-fifteen now. If one of us went down there right away...

tachi-hoshi-ryokan-bath-9.text: I'll go. I was kind of sold on the private bath, honestly, but forty-five minutes for free is hard to argue with.

tachi-hoshi-wine-bill-1.text: So the total's forty-eight thousand six hundred yen, service included. Easiest thing is to just split it three ways, right?

tachi-hoshi-wine-bill-11.text: Okay, I'm paying on the app before anyone does any more math.

tachi-hoshi-wine-bill-2.text: Easiest, sure. Though I'd point out that I had the pasta and tap water.

tachi-hoshi-wine-bill-3.text: And someone, who shall remain nameless, ordered the second bottle of Barolo.

tachi-hoshi-wine-bill-4.text: In my defense, you both had some.

tachi-hoshi-wine-bill-5.text: One glass. Which I'd hardly call splitting a bottle.

tachi-hoshi-wine-bill-6.text: Look, I'm not trying to be petty, but the wine alone came to eighteen thousand yen.

tachi-hoshi-wine-bill-7.text: Fair enough. What if I cover the wine, and we split whatever's left?

tachi-hoshi-wine-bill-9.text: Same. Although, if we're being precise, the dessert was also mostly him.

tachi-im-easy-1.text: So whadda we doin' Sunday? I'm easy.

tachi-im-easy-2.text: There's that craft beer festival in Yokohama. It's supposta be sunny.

tachi-im-easy-3.text: Yokohama's kinduva trek, though, right? An' it'll be packed.

tachi-im-easy-4.text: See, this is what you do. You say you're easy, and then you shoot everything down.

tachi-im-easy-5.text: I'm not shootin' it down! I'm just... raisin' concerns.

tachi-im-easy-7.text: ...Honestly? Stay in, order pizza, and finish that show.

tachi-im-easy-8.text: Ha! Finally. Okay, compromise. The beer festival in the afternoon, back by six, then pizza and the show.

tachi-im-easy-9.text: ...Fine. But we leave at six. Not six-thirty.

tachi-kawa-bbq-sat-1.text: So, we're doing a barbecue at my place on Saturday. You two should come!

tachi-kawa-bbq-sat-2.text: Saturday? Sure, I'm free. I can pick up drinks on the way.

tachi-kawa-bbq-sat-3.text: Oh, that sounds fun. I'll try to make it, but it's kind of a busy weekend.

tachi-kawa-bbq-sat-4.text: Oh, okay. Well, come by whenever.

tachi-kawa-bbq-sat-5.text: Wait, isn't it supposed to rain on Saturday?

tachi-kawa-bbq-sat-6.text: Ugh, you're right. Let's move it to Sunday, then.

tachi-kawa-bbq-sat-7.text: Sunday works for me. I'll still bring the drinks.

tachi-kawa-bbq-sat-8.text: Sunday... I'll have to see. I'll let you know.

tachi-kawa-brunch-booked-1.text: Let's try that new pancake place for brunch on Sunday. Everyone's talking about it.

tachi-kawa-brunch-booked-2.text: I looked it up. They're booked up until next month.

tachi-kawa-brunch-booked-3.text: Then what about the café by the park? You don't need a reservation there.

tachi-kawa-brunch-booked-4.text: The one with the big windows?

tachi-kawa-brunch-booked-5.text: Yeah. But it fills up fast, so we'd have to get there before ten.

tachi-kawa-brunch-booked-6.text: Before ten on a Sunday? I'll try, but I'm not really a morning person.

tachi-kawa-brunch-booked-7.text: Okay, forget the pancakes. I'll go early and grab us a table. Just come when you can.

tachi-kawa-cancel-movie-1.text: Hey, the movie starts at seven-thirty. Are we still meeting at seven?

tachi-kawa-cancel-movie-2.text: About that... I have to stay late at work. I'm so sorry.

tachi-kawa-cancel-movie-3.text: No worries. We can just go without you.

tachi-kawa-cancel-movie-4.text: Or we could push it to the nine-fifteen show.

tachi-kawa-cancel-movie-5.text: Nine-fifteen? I can probably get out of here by eight-thirty.

tachi-kawa-cancel-movie-6.text: Okay, I'm in. Let's not leave anyone out. Nine-fifteen it is.

tachi-kawa-cancel-movie-7.text: I'll change the tickets. Let's meet at the theater at nine.

tachi-kawa-gym-evenings-1.text: I just signed up at the gym by the station. You guys should join too.

tachi-kawa-gym-evenings-2.text: Maybe. How much is it a month?

tachi-kawa-gym-evenings-3.text: Five thousand yen, but it's half off if you sign up with a friend.

tachi-kawa-gym-evenings-5.text: I usually go at six-thirty in the morning, before work.

tachi-kawa-gym-evenings-6.text: Six-thirty? Hmm, I'm not really a morning person. I'll think about it.

tachi-kawa-gym-evenings-7.text: Mornings are hard for me too. Could we go after work instead?

tachi-kawa-gym-evenings-8.text: Sure, I can switch to evenings. Let's say seven, on Tuesdays and Fridays.

tachi-kawa-haneda-bus-1.text: Amy's flight gets into Haneda at eight on Friday. Who can pick her up?

tachi-kawa-haneda-bus-2.text: I'd love to, but I've got a work dinner that night. It might run late.

tachi-kawa-haneda-bus-3.text: I can go. I'll just leave work a little early.

tachi-kawa-haneda-bus-5.text: Yeah. She'll have two big suitcases, though, so let's take a taxi back.

tachi-kawa-haneda-bus-6.text: A taxi from Haneda costs a lot. The airport bus stops right by her hotel.

tachi-kawa-haneda-bus-7.text: Oh, I didn't know that. Okay, the bus it is.

tachi-kawa-haneda-bus-8.text: I'll try to stop by the hotel after dinner and say hi.

tachi-kawa-kamakura-sea-1.text: So, Kamakura or Hakone this Saturday? I'm leaning toward Hakone.

tachi-kawa-kamakura-sea-2.text: Hakone's great, but it's almost two hours each way. Kamakura's only one.

tachi-kawa-kamakura-sea-3.text: I don't mind the train. I just really want to see the ocean.

tachi-kawa-kamakura-sea-4.text: The ocean, huh? Then Kamakura makes more sense. Fine, I'll give up on Hakone.

tachi-kawa-kamakura-sea-5.text: Let's catch the eight-thirty train, before it gets crowded.

tachi-kawa-kamakura-sea-6.text: Sure. I'll pick up some snacks for the ride.

tachi-kawa-kamakura-sea-7.text: Great. Let's meet at the ticket gate at eight-fifteen.

tachi-kawa-lunch-thursday-1.text: Hey, long time no see! We should grab lunch sometime.

tachi-kawa-lunch-thursday-2.text: Yeah, totally. Work's been crazy lately, though.

tachi-kawa-lunch-thursday-3.text: How about Thursday? There's a new taco place that just opened up.

tachi-kawa-lunch-thursday-4.text: Thursday works for me. But I've been staying away from spicy food lately.

tachi-kawa-lunch-thursday-5.text: Oh, okay. Then let's do the sandwich place next door. Their soup's really good.

tachi-kawa-lunch-thursday-6.text: Thursday's kind of tough for me. Let me check and get back to you.

tachi-kawa-lunch-thursday-7.text: No worries. We'll be there at twelve if you can make it.

tachi-kawa-parcel-drop-1.text: My new chair is getting delivered tomorrow, but I'll be out all day.

tachi-kawa-parcel-drop-2.text: Can't you just have them leave it at the door?

tachi-kawa-parcel-drop-3.text: It's a big box. Someone has to sign for it.

tachi-kawa-parcel-drop-4.text: I'm home in the morning. I could sign for it, if it's early.

tachi-kawa-parcel-drop-5.text: It says between one and five, though.

tachi-kawa-parcel-drop-6.text: Oh, then I'll do it. I work from home in the afternoon.

tachi-kawa-parcel-drop-7.text: Perfect. I can drop by later and help you carry it up.

tachi-kawa-parcel-drop-8.text: You guys are the best. Dinner's on me this weekend.

tachi-kawa-potluck-bread-1.text: So for the potluck on Saturday, I'm making my lasagna.

tachi-kawa-potluck-bread-2.text: Nice. I wanted to bake bread, but I'm working until three.

tachi-kawa-potluck-bread-3.text: Then just pick up some bread on the way. Nobody will mind.

tachi-kawa-potluck-bread-4.text: Yeah, I guess you're right. I'll grab some from the bakery by the station.

tachi-kawa-potluck-bread-5.text: I'll bring a salad. And plates, since we always run out of them.

tachi-kawa-potluck-bread-6.text: Perfect. Oh, and can someone bring ice? My freezer's tiny.

tachi-kawa-potluck-bread-7.text: I'll take care of it. Bread and ice.

tachi-kawa-van-move-1.text: I'm moving next Saturday, and the movers want sixty thousand yen. That's crazy.

tachi-kawa-van-move-2.text: Just rent a van. I can help you carry stuff.

tachi-kawa-van-move-3.text: I'd help too, but my back's been acting up again.

tachi-kawa-van-move-4.text: A van? But I've never driven in Tokyo.

tachi-kawa-van-move-5.text: Oh, don't worry about that. I'll drive. It's only about ten thousand yen for the day.

tachi-kawa-van-move-6.text: Ten thousand? Okay, that changes things. Let's forget the movers.

tachi-kawa-van-move-7.text: I can still help you pack boxes on Friday night. I'll bring pizza.

tachi-launch-hedge-1.text: So, the client wants ta move the launch up to March first. Is that doable?

tachi-launch-hedge-2.text: It might be tricky. I mean, it's not impossible, but we'd be cuttin' corners on testing.

tachi-launch-hedge-3.text: Tricky? Come on, we're already behind. There's no way we're ready by March.

tachi-launch-hedge-4.text: They're offering a bonus if we hit it, apparently. Twenty percent on top.

tachi-launch-hedge-5.text: ...Okay, twenty percent's not nothin'. If we drop the Android version for launch, maybe.

tachi-launch-hedge-6.text: I'm not crazy about dropping Android. Half their users are on it.

tachi-launch-hedge-7.text: What if Android follows two weeks later? I can sell them on that.

tachi-launch-hedge-8.text: Fine. I O S on the first, Android by the fifteenth. But I want that in writing.

tachi-leaving-gift-1.text: Okay, Dana's going-away party is Friday, and we're standing in Target with no plan. I was thinking a nice bottle of wine.

tachi-leaving-gift-2.text: She doesn't drink, though, does she? I've never seen 'er have anything stronger than iced tea.

tachi-leaving-gift-3.text: Yeah, no, wine's a bad call. An' not a gift card, either. That's whatcha get yer mail carrier.

tachi-leaving-gift-4.text: Ugh, but a gift card's so easy. There's a whole wall of 'em right there, by checkout.

tachi-leaving-gift-5.text: She's movin' to Denver for the hiking, isn't she? Get 'er something for that. Camping stuff's in the back.

tachi-leaving-gift-6.text: Ooh, a good thermos. An' the place in the mall can engrave the team name on it.

tachi-leaving-gift-7.text: Okay, I'm sold. A thermos from here, engraved at the mall. If we drop it off today, it's ready Thursday.

tachi-leaving-gift-8.text: You're the best. I'll grab a card and get everyone to sign it.

tachi-movers-or-truck-1.text: So, the move's on the twenty-eighth. Do we rent a truck, or just pay movers?

tachi-movers-or-truck-2.text: Truck. Movers quoted me eight hundred bucks. A truck's like ninety fer the day.

tachi-movers-or-truck-3.text: Sure, an' who's carryin' the couch down four flights of stairs? Not me.

tachi-movers-or-truck-4.text: We'll get the guys from soccer. Pizza an' beer, done.

tachi-movers-or-truck-5.text: Las' time ya said that, two of 'em flaked an' you threw yer back out.

tachi-movers-or-truck-6.text: What if we do both? Movers jus' for the big stuff, an' we drive the boxes ourselves.

tachi-movers-or-truck-7.text: Huh. That's, what, half the price? Okay, yeah, my back says yes.

tachi-movers-or-truck-8.text: Great. I'll call 'em fer a quote on jus' the couch, the bed an' the fridge.

tachi-noisy-neighbour-1.text: Did either of you hear the guy in four-oh-five last night? Drilling. At midnight.

tachi-noisy-neighbour-2.text: I did. I was gonna go up an' say something, but I didn't wanna make it awkward.

tachi-noisy-neighbour-3.text: Honestly, I'd just leave a note at the management office. Let 'em deal with it.

tachi-noisy-neighbour-4.text: A note? He'll never know it's about 'im. I say we just knock on 'is door.

tachi-noisy-neighbour-5.text: I'd rather not knock. He's huge.

tachi-noisy-neighbour-6.text: He's actually really nice. He helped me carry my bike up last week. He probably just doesn't realize how thin the walls are.

tachi-noisy-neighbour-7.text: Oh. Well, if he's nice... maybe a friendly word is better than a note, then.

tachi-noisy-neighbour-8.text: Great. We'll go up together after work. Safety in numbers.

tachi-office-days-1.text: So did you see the email? Three days a week in the office starting in April.

tachi-office-days-2.text: I saw. I don't mind, to be honest. I get more done here than at home with the cat on my keyboard.

tachi-office-days-3.text: That's 'cause you live ten minutes away. My commute's an hour an' a half each way.

tachi-office-days-4.text: Same. And for what? To sit on video calls with the Fukuoka office?

tachi-office-days-5.text: Fair point. Although it's nice to actually see people. I'd forgotten what you two looked like.

tachi-office-days-6.text: Okay, I'll admit the coffee's better here. But three days is too many. Two, I could live with.

tachi-office-days-7.text: Let's put that in the team survey, then. Two days, flexible.

tachi-office-days-8.text: Fine, I'll back it. But I'm still comin' in four.

tachi-parents-visit-1.text: So Mom and Dad land on the ninth. Are they staying with us, or should I book a hotel?

tachi-parents-visit-2.text: With us, obviously. Mom'd be so hurt if we put 'em in a hotel.

tachi-parents-visit-3.text: Marshal, ya have a studio. Where's Dad gonna sleep, the bathtub?

tachi-parents-visit-4.text: My place has the spare room, but the bed's really jus' a futon on the floor. Dad's back can't take that.

tachi-parents-visit-5.text: There's a business hotel two minutes from yer station. Clean, cheap, an' they'd still eat dinner with us every night.

tachi-parents-visit-6.text: Every night? Okay... if we do dinner together every night, Mom won't feel shut out. Fine, hotel.

tachi-parents-visit-7.text: I'll book it tanight. Six nights, the ninth through the fifteenth.

tachi-parents-visit-8.text: An' I'll pick 'em up at the airport. Marshal, you're on dinner reservations.

tachi-pub-quiz-1.text: Question seven. Which country has the most time zones? We've got thirty seconds.

tachi-pub-quiz-3.text: It's France, actually. Because of all the overseas territories. Twelve, I think.

tachi-pub-quiz-4.text: France? Come on. That's a trick answer.

tachi-pub-quiz-5.text: No, I think he's right. I read that somewhere. Tahiti an' stuff.

tachi-pub-quiz-6.text: Ugh, fine. But if it's Russia, you're both buyin' the next round.

tachi-pub-quiz-8.text: Quick, quick, they're collecting the answer sheets!

tachi-rental-compact-1.text: So the rental place says the compact's ready, but the S U V won't be back till three.

tachi-rental-compact-2.text: Three? We'd hit Friday traffic outta the city. Let's jus' take the compact.

tachi-rental-compact-3.text: With three suitcases an' the cooler? We won't fit. I'm not ridin' with a cooler on my lap fer four hours.

tachi-rental-compact-4.text: We could ship the suitcases ahead. The hotel takes deliveries.

tachi-rental-compact-5.text: Oh, nice. So it's jus' the cooler an' our backpacks. That fits easy.

tachi-rental-compact-6.text: Fine, if the bags go ahead, the compact's okay. But I'm not drivin' the mountain part.

tachi-rental-compact-7.text: I'll take the mountain part. Dom, ya drive us outta the city, an' we leave at noon.

tachi-rental-compact-8.text: Noon it is. I'll drop the suitcases at the convenience store on the way.

tachi-school-choice-1.text: The international school's open house was incredible. Small classes, all in English, an' a robotics lab.

tachi-school-choice-2.text: It was. It was also two an' a half million yen a year. Per kid. Before the bus.

tachi-school-choice-3.text: Can I just say, as the one who pays fer nothing: she'll be livin' here. If she can't talk to the kids on 'er street, that's lonely.

tachi-school-choice-4.text: But her Japanese is still shaky. I don't want 'er sittin' in a class understandin' nothing.

tachi-school-choice-5.text: Kids that age pick it up in, like, six months. Adults are the ones who struggle. Present company included...

tachi-school-choice-6.text: An' the public school near you has that Saturday English club. She'd get both.

tachi-school-choice-7.text: ...Okay. If she's strugglin' after a term, we revisit. But I'm willin' ta try the local school.

tachi-school-choice-8.text: Deal. I'll call the ward office Monday about enrollment.

tachi-second-opinion-1.text: So Dad's surgeon wants ta do the full knee replacement next month. He says the sooner, the better.

tachi-second-opinion-2.text: Next month? He only started physical therapy in March. That feels like jumpin' the gun.

tachi-second-opinion-3.text: I'm with Cyrano. Not sayin' the guy's wrong, but fer something this big, Dad should get a second opinion.

tachi-second-opinion-4.text: Honestly, I jus' want 'im outta pain. He can barely do the stairs. A second opinion could take, what, six weeks ta book?

tachi-second-opinion-5.text: Not necessarily. My friend's clinic does video consults. They'd look at 'is scans this week.

tachi-second-opinion-6.text: This week? Oh. Well, if it doesn't push the surgery back, then sure, I've got no problem with a second look.

tachi-second-opinion-7.text: Even if they agree, at least Dad goes in knowin' it's the right call. That's worth a week.

tachi-second-opinion-8.text: I'll text 'er tanight an' send the scans. Melba, can ya tell Dad? He listens ta you.

tachi-shibuya-dinner-1.text: Okay, it's almost eight. Are we doin' ramen or what?

tachi-shibuya-dinner-2.text: I'm still up for ramen. That place by the station's open late.

tachi-shibuya-dinner-3.text: Not ramen again. We had it on Tuesday. Whaddabout that izakaya with the yakitori?

tachi-shibuya-dinner-4.text: The one up the hill? You'd need a reservation there on a Friday, fer sure.

tachi-shibuya-dinner-5.text: I'll call them. Worst case, they say no.

tachi-shibuya-dinner-6.text: Actually, yeah, yakitori sounds good. I could go for a beer anyway.

tachi-shibuya-dinner-7.text: Fine by me, as long as we're not waitin' an hour. If they're full, it's ramen, no arguments.

tachi-standup-blocked-1.text: Okay, quick round. Agnes, you first.

tachi-standup-blocked-2.text: Yesterday I finished the login screens. Today I'm on the payment flow, but I'm stuck till I get the new A P I keys from Lucky's team.

tachi-standup-blocked-3.text: Yeah, about that. Security hasn't signed off on 'em yet. Could be Thursday.

tachi-standup-blocked-5.text: I know, I know. I'll bug 'em this mornin'. Worst case, she c'n use the test keys for the demo.

tachi-standup-blocked-6.text: Test keys won't show the real card screen, though. That's the whole point of the demo.

tachi-standup-blocked-7.text: Okay, then let's not risk it. We push the demo to Friday, an' I'll tell the client. Lucky, keys by Thursday, no later.

tachi-surprise-party-1.text: Okay, so the cake's getting picked up at five, and the restaurant's holding the back room from seven.

tachi-surprise-party-2.text: An' she still thinks we're just havin' a quiet dinner, right? Not twenty people.

tachi-surprise-party-3.text: Hang on. Who's pickin' up the cake? I thought you said you would.

tachi-surprise-party-4.text: I said I'd order it. I can't do five, I'm at the hair salon till five-thirty.

tachi-surprise-party-5.text: I'll get it, then. It's on my way.

tachi-surprise-party-6.text: Wait, no, you're the one taking her to the restaurant. You can't show up with a cake box.

tachi-surprise-party-7.text: Good point. Fine, you do the cake, then.

tachi-surprise-party-8.text: Shh! She's here. So, uh, yes, the report's due Monday, everyone.

tachi-thirtieth-1.text: Okay, Yui's thirtieth. I've narrowed it down to three. Karaoke, the rooftop bar in Ebisu, or that omakase place.

tachi-thirtieth-2.text: Omakase's twenty thousand a head. For ten people? That's a stretch.

tachi-thirtieth-3.text: Karaoke, obviously. She's been talkin' about doin' Celine Dion for weeks.

tachi-thirtieth-4.text: I dunno, karaoke feels kinda... last year. The rooftop has a view, an' it's only five thousand with a drink.

tachi-thirtieth-5.text: A rooftop in November? Okay, but I'm bringin' a jacket.

tachi-thirtieth-6.text: They have heaters, too. And blankets.

tachi-thirtieth-7.text: Okay, what if we do the rooftop first, then karaoke after? Everybody's happy.

tachi-thirtieth-8.text: Now that I can get behind. As long as I'm not doing a duet.

tachi-train-tourists-1.text: So is it this stop or the next one for the big temple?

tachi-train-tourists-2.text: Asakusa? We're not even on the right line for that. This is goin' to Shinjuku.

tachi-train-tourists-3.text: Which is fine, because we said Shinjuku Gyoen first, didn't we? The garden. Then the temple tomorrow.

tachi-train-tourists-4.text: Did we? I thought the garden was closed on Mondays.

tachi-train-tourists-6.text: Is it? Wow. Okay. Garden it is.

tachi-train-tourists-7.text: Then we want Shinjuku-gyoemmae, not Shinjuku. Which means changin' at Yotsuya. That's... two stops from here.

tachi-two-seats-1.text: Okay, folks, unfortunately the Singapore connection already left. I've got two seats on the eleven-forty tonight, and that's it.

tachi-two-seats-2.text: I'll take one. I've got a meetin' at nine tomorrow.

tachi-two-seats-3.text: Sorry, I was actually here first. An' I've got a toddler with me.

tachi-two-seats-4.text: Ma'am, with your little one, you'd need both seats.

tachi-two-seats-5.text: Which leaves me with nothing. Fantastic.

tachi-two-seats-6.text: Not quite, sir. There's a seven a m tomorrow through Hong Kong, an' I can get you into the lounge tonight.

tachi-two-seats-7.text: The lounge? With a shower? ...Actually, that's not bad. I'll move the meeting.

tachi-two-seats-8.text: Thank you. Seriously. I owe you a drink.

tachi-urgent-care-1.text: It's fine, it's jus' a little swollen. I'll put some ice on it an' sleep it off.

tachi-urgent-care-2.text: Dude, it's the size of a grapefruit. Ya can't even put yer shoe on.

tachi-urgent-care-3.text: I'd go to urgent care, not the E R. The E R's gonna be a four-hour wait on a Saturday night.

tachi-urgent-care-4.text: Urgent care is like a hundred an' fifty bucks without insurance, though.

tachi-urgent-care-5.text: You have insurance. Through work. Ya literally showed me the card las' month.

tachi-urgent-care-6.text: Oh. Right. Okay, fine, if it's covered, I'll go. But I'm not goin' in an ambulance.

tachi-urgent-care-7.text: Nobody said ambulance. The one on Fifth closes at ten, so we should leave now.

tachi-urgent-care-8.text: I'll drive. Phoebe, grab 'is insurance card an' a bag of frozen peas.

tile-hoshi-commute-old.text: It's not a dealbreaker, but that commute would get old fast.

tile-hoshi-defeats-point.text: Check-in isn't till three, which defeats the whole point.

tile-hoshi-deposit-catch.text: What the movers didn't mention is that the deposit's nonrefundable after Friday.

tile-hoshi-dessert-bite.text: Dessert sounds amazing, but I'll probably just have a bite of yours.

tile-hoshi-easy-traffic.text: I'm easy, as long as we don't spend Saturday stuck in traffic.

tile-hoshi-elevator-isnt.text: The quote assumes there's an elevator, which there isn't.

tile-hoshi-fine-to-fly.text: You should be fine to fly, provided the swelling goes down.

tile-hoshi-for-granted.text: Honestly, it sounds like they've been taking you for granted.

tile-hoshi-had-i-known.text: Had I known the ferry was canceled, I'd have taken the train.

tile-hoshi-high-school-play.text: I've seen better acting at a high school play, no offense.

tile-hoshi-hold-drop-off.text: The hold on your card should drop off within five business days.

tile-hoshi-holding-breath.text: He swears it'll be fixed soon, not that I'm holding my breath.

tile-hoshi-in-your-shoes.text: I'd have said something too, if I'd been in your shoes.

tile-hoshi-lobster-tip.text: Since you had the lobster, you can cover the tip.

tile-hoshi-masterpiece.text: It was a masterpiece, if you like falling asleep halfway through.

tile-hoshi-nine-hour-layover.text: The only flight that gets us there tonight has a nine-hour layover.

tile-hoshi-not-on-us.text: Apparently the leak's coming from upstairs, so it's not even on us.

tile-hoshi-number-stomach.text: Take it with food, or it'll do a number on your stomach.

tile-hoshi-off-carbs.text: Normally I'd jump at it, but I'm off carbs for now.

tile-hoshi-rash-reassess.text: If the rash hasn't cleared up by Monday, we'll reassess.

ya-r-quick-sync.text: Oh, great, another quick sync at six p.m. on a Friday. My favorite.

ya-r-rain-check.text: Saturday's kinda up in the air for me. Can we just play it by ear?

ya-r-sleep-on.text: It's a really generous offer. Would it be okay if I slept on it?

ya-r-under-bus.text: Didja seriously just throw me under the bus in fronna the whole team?

ya-r-whaddaya.text: Whaddaya say we just order in an' call it a night?

ya-w-coulda.text: It coulda been way worse, honestly.

ya-w-couldja.text: Couldja grab me one while you're up?

ya-w-get-it.text: He's gotta get it done by Monday.

ya-w-gimme.text: Gimme a sec, I'm almost done with this level.

ya-w-hafta.text: If we're catchin' the last train, we hafta leave by eleven-thirty.

ya-w-ida.text: I'da told ya if I'da known.

ya-w-not-gonna-lie.text: I'm not gonna lie, that was rough.

ya-w-oughta.text: You oughta get that looked at. It's been weeks.

ya-w-sorta.text: I sorta forgot ta call 'er back.

ya-w-tell-im.text: If he calls, just tell 'im I'm in a meeting.

ya-w-useta.text: We useta come here every summer when I was a kid.

ya-w-whaddaya.text: Whaddaya think of the new guy, honestly?

ya-w-wouldnt-wanna.text: Trust me, you wouldn't wanna be there at rush hour.

ya-w-you-gonna.text: You gonna eat that, or can I have it?

yb-agree-to-disagree.text: I think we're going around in circles. Can we just agree to disagree and move on?

yb-anywhere-near.text: AI's great for a first draft. I just wouldn't let it anywhere near the final version.

yb-authorize.text: I'd love to give you Friday off, but that's above my pay grade. I can ask the boss for you, though.

yb-back-order.text: The parts are on back order, so we're lookin' at six to eight weeks, not the two we said.

yb-barely-warm.text: Excuse me, sorry to be a pain, but this is barely warm in the middle.

yb-base-salary.text: The base is ninety-two K, with up to fifteen percent bonus, so in a good year, just over a hundred and five.

yb-bearer.text: I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but your car's not gonna be ready till Monday.

yb-before-midnight.text: Don't get me wrong, I love a little music. I'd just love it a lot more before midnight.

yb-break-fee.text: Break the lease in the first year and there's a fee of two months' rent, so thirty-eight hundred bucks.

yb-business-days.text: Once we get the form, it's three to five business days for review, then another ten for the card to arrive.

yb-cant-face.text: Kyoto's beautiful, but honestly, I can't deal with the crowds at Fushimi Inari again.

yb-check-in-closes.text: Check-in closes forty-five minutes before departure, so with a seven-fifteen flight, you'll wanna be through by six-thirty.

yb-coming-from.text: I see where you're coming from, but I'm not sure the numbers back that up.

yb-could-have-email.text: Wow. Ninety minutes, and it coulda been one email.

yb-couldnt-agree.text: Honestly, I couldn't agree more, but that's not the part I'm worried about.

yb-cut-back.text: I'm not saying cut it out altogether. Just maybe not three coffees before lunch.

yb-decision-maker.text: I appreciate you're only following policy, but I'd like to speak to someone who can actually make a decision.

yb-deductions.text: Your first paycheck looks small because of all the deductions for health insurance and taxes.

yb-deposit-hold.text: We'll put a hold of four-fifty on your card, which drops to one-fifty if you take the full coverage.

yb-devils-advocate.text: Just to play devil's advocate, are we sure customers actually want this, or do we just want to build it?

yb-didnt-include.text: Just so you know, the quote didn' include tax or delivery.

yb-different-direction.text: Thanks so much for your time. The team really enjoyed meeting you, but we decided to go in a different direction.

yb-double-check.text: You might wanna double-check that figure before it goes to the client.

yb-double-seven.text: Your case number is five-oh-seven, seven-one-three. That's two sevens in the middle.

yb-due-respect.text: With all due respect, that's not what was agreed in the last meeting.

yb-electric-bill.text: The electric bill's eleven thousand eight hundred this month, almost double last month's six thousand two hundred. It's the heater.

yb-escalated.text: I've passed your question on to the head coach. She usually gets back to parents within forty-eight hours.

yb-fill-out.text: Just fill out the top half 'n' leave the rest to us.

yb-final-offer.text: Look, I'll be straight with ya. That's my final offer, and between you and me, there's another buyer comin' at four.

yb-generously.text: Right. So I ordered a king-size, and what's turned up is, generously, a large single.

yb-get-noticed.text: Purple for a law firm's logo? Well, it'll certainly get noticed.

yb-go-for.text: If you had to pick one, the ryokan in Hakone or the hotel in Yokohama, which would you go for?

yb-good-on-you.text: Cold plunges? Hey, if it works for you, more power to you. I'll stick to a hot bath.

yb-goodwill.text: I can't fix it for free, but since it's you, I'll knock the price down to half.

yb-hasnt-gone.text: Hey, your Venmo for the cabin hasn' come through on my end.

yb-headcount.text: We're at thirty-eight sign-ups, minus the five who canceled, plus the three from the Denver office.

yb-hit-pause.text: Let's hit pause on pricing till legal's taken a look. No point locking anything in before then.

yb-in-theory.text: Remote work's great in theory. In practice, I end up answering emails at eleven at night.

yb-last-four.text: Before I can do anything, I'll just need you to verify the last four digits of the card.

yb-launch-date.text: Before we wrap up, are we all on the same page about the launch date?

yb-make-sense.text: So you scan it, tag it, and then it goes to finance for sign-off. Does that make sense?

yb-match-quote.text: The company down the road quoted us twelve hundred for the same job. Can you match that?

yb-max-dose.text: Take two tonight, then one every eight hours, but no more than six in twenty-four hours.

yb-might-as-well.text: Honestly, you might's well wait for the sale at this point.

yb-mustnt-drive.text: You mussn't drive for twenty-four hours after the sedation.

yb-not-go-ahead.text: Unfortunately, the board decided not to go ahead with the project, at least for this year.

yb-not-liable.text: If anything gets broken while we're moving it, we're not liable unless you've bought the extra coverage.

yb-notice-period.text: You're welcome to take her out of the program, of course. It's just that we require a full month's notice, and we'd need that in writing.

yb-on-hold.text: I'm gonna have to restart your phone in recovery mode, and anything that isn't backed up is gone. Is that OK?

yb-on-me.text: You got the last round, so this one's on me. And no, I'm not taking no for an answer.

yb-ought-to.text: You oughta book your tickets early. They tend to sell out by Friday.

yb-overcharged.text: I was quoted seventy-nine a month, but I've been charged ninety-seven for three months now.

yb-park-that.text: Can we park that for now and come back to it once we've seen the budget?

yb-rent-up.text: From April, the swim club fee goes up from eight thousand two hundred to eight thousand nine hundred and fifty a month.

yb-role-affected.text: As you know, we've been reviewing the team structure, and unfortunately, your role is one of the ones affected.

yb-rule-out.text: It's probably nothing to worry about, but I'd like to rule a few things out, so I'm gonna order some blood work.

yb-run-it-by.text: So, can we shake on twelve percent, or d'you need to run it by your team first?

yb-running-behind.text: The doctor's running about forty minutes behind. Are you okay to wait, or would you rather reschedule?

yb-saitama-or-central.text: Would you rather have a bigger place out in Saitama, or something tiny in central Tokyo?

yb-sign-today.text: We'd need you to sign today to lock in this rate.

yb-sit-tight.text: I mean, it's your call, but if it were my money, I'd probably sit tight till the new model's out.

yb-skip-step.text: You can skip step four, technically. I just wouldn't, unless you enjoy starting again from scratch.

yb-small-print.text: Read the fine print, man. There's a twelve-month minimum, and they charge you to leave early.

yb-split-four.text: The Airbnb was eleven-forty for three nights, plus a sixty-dollar cleaning fee, split four ways.

yb-sprain.text: Good news: it's a sprain rather than a break, so you'll be back on your feet in a couple of weeks.

yb-supposed-to.text: We were s'posta leave at noon. It's two, and you're still packing.

yb-sweeten.text: If you can sign by Friday, I might be able to get my manager to sweeten the deal a little.

yb-table-it.text: Let's table this until Thursday, when the whole team's there.

yb-take-home.text: On paper it's three hundred eighty thousand, but after tax and insurance I take home about two hundred ninety thousand.

yb-tell-them.text: Call the office and tell 'em it's been three days, and ask for something stronger.

yb-that-fly.text: Noted. I'm not sure that'll fly with the client, but let's see what they say.

yb-third-time.text: This is the third time this week the dishes have sat in the sink overnight, and every time you say you'll get to them.

yb-throw-in.text: I can't go any lower on the rate, but I could throw in the installation for free.

yb-too-soon.text: It's not that the plan's bad. I just think we're trying to do too much, too soon.

yb-tourists.text: Apparently somethin' like thirty-six million tourists came last year, and half of them were in my neighborhood konbini.

yb-whos-owning.text: So who's owning the follow-up with the vendor?

yb-wiggle-room.text: Honestly, that's a little outside what we'd budgeted. If there's any wiggle room on your end, we'd love to make this work.

yb-wont-be-able.text: I'm sorry, but we won't be able to fit you in until next month.

yb-working-days.text: Your new card should arrive in seven to ten business days, but you can start using it in the app today.

yb-wouldve-split.text: Oh, come on, I woulda split it with ya if you'd just asked.
